post.description:
Confirms a fulfillment that is in a pending state. Some marketplace fulfillment flows require an explicit confirmation step before the shipment is processed downstream.

**When to use:** Call this endpoint after creating a fulfillment (`POST /v1/Fulfillments`) when the marketplace or workflow requires a manual confirmation step before the shipment is dispatched.

**Considerations:**
- Confirm only after verifying that all fulfillment items are available and ready to ship.
- Confirming a fulfillment that is not in a confirmable state returns an error.
- This operation may trigger downstream marketplace notifications.

post.description:
Denies a pending fulfillment. Use this endpoint when a fulfillment cannot be completed as planned — for example, when items are unavailable at the distribution center or a pickup was not collected by the customer.

**When to use:** Call this endpoint before the fulfillment is confirmed or shipped, when you need to cancel or reject the fulfillment.

**Considerations:**
- Denying a fulfillment may trigger marketplace-specific cancellation workflows and buyer notifications.
- A denied fulfillment cannot be un-denied. Create a new fulfillment if the order still needs to be fulfilled.
- Only applicable to fulfillments in a deniable state; returns an error otherwise.

get.description:
> Note:
> Webhooks available
> Orders can be delivered via Webhooks - check out the documentation on available events.

* Make sure to read through Getting and Filtering Data and all subsections on this page to understand what retrieval standards the REST API supports.
* All dates in the REST API are UTC, while the web application dates are time-zone specific (to the profile time zone setting).
* Order data differs from one marketplace to the next - as a result, some properties may be populated, while others are null or blank.
* Response data is limited to a maximum of 100 orders at a time.
  * To maintain efficient processing through multiple pages of orders, use the @odata.nextLink at the bottom of the response - do not hardcode $skip values. See more about Paging Through Results.
* Expanding collections in a general orders retrieval (GET /v1/Orders endpoint) will result in a maximum of 100 items per collection.
  * For example, if there are more than 100 items in an order, only the first 100 will appear in the initial response data.
  * Be prepared to page through items is required using the @odata.nextLink links at the end of each Collection section (this includes the OrderItems entity within the Order, and FulfillmentItems entity within the Fulfillment).
    * In requests without extensive filtering criteria, all items will appear in the response and will not require paging.
    * Alternately retrieve orders with more than 100 items directly by requesting the order directly (GET /v1/Orders(OrderID)) and expanding collections - all items will be displayed in that response.
* Important data may exist in the PublicNotes, PrivateNotes, and SpecialInstructions fields, but can be updated by the seller as needed.
  * Recommend appending changes, rather than overwriting to these fields to ensure the original data in these fields is not lost.
* To build out an efficient and faster integration, we recommend using Export status as a way to mark orders already received/imported.
  * Using $filter and any date fields as a way to limit what orders are imported is generally inefficient.
* The platform acknowledges the orders back to the marketplace on the seller's behalf within the allotted timeframe - no acknowledgement request is required by the seller.
* Do not code to specific HTTP response values - these may change. Code to the range if possible (e.g. 200 values are successful responses; 400 values are improperly formatted requests; 500 values are platform-side server errors).
* Add $count=true to the request URI to retrieve the total number of orders matching the query.
  * Warning: requesting the count may increase response times by up to 100%, so when paging through results, it is highly recommended to only request the count with the first page, if at all.
 

### Property information
* Property types
  * Most property types (e.g. 'string' length, integer as 32 bit) are much longer than values we receive from any marketplaces. This is done to accommodate changes that the marketplaces may make.
  * We recommend development plans be similarly flexible because marketplaces can change the values/formats they use at any time without notice.
* PrivateNotes may contain data from different marketplaces - be sure to get this data before updating it. It may be relevant to business reporting.
* Shipping Carrier and Shipping Classvalues differ from one marketplace to the next. Find a list of values to expect from each marketplace - if a marketplace doesn't exist in this link, Contact Us by creating a Support case.
  * The values returned to the marketplace can be customized based on system settings and needs.
  * A seller will need to set up custom shipping carrier/classes (or coordinate with contacts at Rithum) in the web application.
* Site Names (and Site IDs)will be static for each marketplace over time. Contact Us by creating a Support case if a marketplace you need to know about doesn't exist.
* OrderTags
  * OrderTags may be populated with referential data generated by Rithum, but cannot be set via API requests with POST/PATCH/PUT.
  * Not filterable.
* Distribution center type rollup
  * Provides a filterable value representing a summary of the distribution center types that are referenced in the Fulfillments collection in an order.
  * Recommend use of these values to limit orders to Seller Managed or Externally Managed Distribution Centers.
* Distribution center IDs
  * Only exists under the Fulfillments collection.
  * Only relevant if multiple distribution centers exist in a Rithum integration.
  * Quantity is set at the Fulfillment level, and the product's Distribution Center ID may be relevant. When retrieving orders, make sure $expand=Fulfillments is added to the URL see the DistributionCenterID value.
  * Read more about Distribution Centers and accessing DistributionCenterIDs.
* External fulfillment center codes
  * Exists under the Fulfillments collection.
  * Only relevant to Amazon FBA (Fulfillment by Amazon) orders
  * Does not apply to Multi-Channel FBA orders
  * Values are provided exactly as the marketplace defines them
 
### General expected behavior
* Required properties - many POST/PATCH endpoints only require the data point(s) intended to send, so there may be very few required fields in examples. See the Order Entity tables for POST and PATCH requirements.
* Order Item information that comes from the marketplace may not match what exists in our inventory - for example: "Title" will be the value presented by the marketplace to the platform at the time the order was received, and will not necessarily match any title field in the platform.
* Orders data and Product data are independent in our databases, and therefore no single request exists to retrieve Order data and Product-specific data points/attributes/etc.
  * We are constantly reviewing and expanding our capabilities, so some Product data points may become available within Orders in the future.
* Order frequency
  * See Marketplace Communication Frequency to find out how often we'll import data from each marketplace, and send refunds/cancellations back to the marketplace.
* For most marketplaces - orders are ready to be retrieved from the platform when:
  * PaymentStatus = "Cleared" AND CheckoutStatus = "Completed"
  * These two statuses indicate the marketplace has successfully processed the order and completed fraud checks (when applicable)
* Pending Orders do not exist for most marketplaces - Amazon is one exception. Read through this linked page for more information about how to handle pending orders.
 
### Retrieve order endpoints
| Endpoint | Descriptions |
|----------|-------------|
| GET /v1/Orders |	Query against all orders across accounts |
| GET /v1/Orders(id)|	Retrieve a single order |
| GET /v1/Orders(id)/Items|	Retrieve all items for a single order |

> Note: When filters on exported status, PaymentStatus, or ShippingStatus are used, Rithum provides an optimized response limited to the last 30 days of orders data. This could impact your $count. If date filters are included in the request, that filter will be respected and the 30 day limit will be ignored.

Paid and Unshipped orders.value: PaymentStatus eq PaymentCleared and ShippingStatus eq Unshipped

Confirms receipt of an order from a marketplace. Some marketplaces (such as Amazon) require sellers to acknowledge orders within a specified time window — failing to confirm within this window may result in automatic cancellation by the marketplace.

**When to use:** Call this endpoint after retrieving an order to acknowledge that you have accepted it and intend to fulfil it.

**Considerations:**
- Rithum typically handles acknowledgement automatically for most marketplaces. Call this endpoint only if your workflow requires manual confirmation.
- This endpoint is idempotent — calling it more than once on an already-confirmed order has no adverse effect.
- Not all marketplaces require explicit confirmation; check marketplace-specific guidance if unsure.

post.description:
Denies (rejects) an order from a marketplace. Use this endpoint when you are unable to fulfil an order — for example, when the item is out of stock or you cannot ship to the buyer's address.

**When to use:** Call this endpoint before any items are shipped to notify the marketplace that you cannot fulfil the order. The marketplace will typically cancel the order and notify the buyer.

**Considerations:**
- Only deny an order that has not yet been (partially) shipped. Denying a shipped order results in an error.
- Not all marketplaces support order denial; behaviour varies by marketplace.
- Once denied, the order cannot be un-denied. Contact the buyer and/or marketplace support if you need to reverse a denial.

post.description:
Buys a shipping label using a `RateID` returned by `ShippingRates`.

**When to use:** Second step of the two-step workflow, after `ShippingRates`.

**Considerations:**
- The only parameters are `RateID`, `LabelFormat`, and `ShippingLabelRequestID`.
- `LabelFormat` is required (`PDF` or `ZPL`); omitting it returns 400 "LabelFormat is required."
- An expired or unknown `RateID` returns 400. A rate is deleted from the cache once it has been purchased.
- Reusing a `ShippingLabelRequestID` returns the existing label.
- Purchasing a label marks the items shipped: it creates a shipped fulfillment with the carrier, class, `ShippedDateUTC`, tracking number, and delivery status `Complete` (partial shipment), then saves the label.
- Success returns 200 multipart/mixed: a JSON part that describes the fulfillment (for example its ID and tracking number), followed by the label.

See the Shipping Labels guide for the full two-step workflow.

LabelFormat.description: The format of the shipping label. Required. Must be `PDF` or `ZPL`; omitting it returns 400 "LabelFormat is required."

200.description: The label was purchased (or the existing label for the `ShippingLabelRequestID` was returned). The body is multipart/mixed: a JSON part that describes the fulfillment (for example its ID and tracking number), followed by the label.

post.description:
Returns shipping rates for the items of an order, and optionally buys the cheapest one.

**When to use:** To price a label before buying it (then call `PurchaseLabel` with a `RateID`), or to buy the cheapest rate in one call with `PurchaseCheapestRate: true`.

**Considerations:**
- `Items` is required (at least one item), and each quantity must be greater than 0. `LabelFormat` must be `PDF` or `ZPL`.
- `Weight`, `WeightUnit`, `MeasurementUnit`, the package dimensions, `DistributionCenterID`, and `PackageID` are optional in the request schema. Dimensions come from `PackageID` if present, otherwise from height, length, and width provided together. An unknown `DistributionCenterID` or `PackageID` returns 400 ("DistributionCenterID N does not exist." / "PackageID N does not exist.").
- How `DeliveryConfirmation` is applied depends on the shipping partner.
- `LabelFormat` defaults to `PDF`. `DeliveryConfirmation` defaults to `NoDeliveryConfirmation`.
- Each rate has a `RateID` valid for 1800 seconds (`ExpiresInSeconds`).
- `ShippingLabelRequestID` (max 50 characters) identifies the request. Reusing an ID that was already used to buy a label returns the cached rates (kept 30 days) and, only with `PurchaseCheapestRate`, the purchased label.
- `PurchaseCheapestRate` buys only when rates exist and there are no errors; media/library mail is excluded. Already-shipped items are rejected with `PurchaseCheapestRate`. The purchase marks the items shipped, as with `PurchaseLabel`.
- `PurchaseCheapestRate` requires the request to resolve to a single shipping partner (several accounts of the same partner are fine). With more than one partner it fails with 400 ("PurchaseCheapestRate cannot be used when more than one shipping partner is used."); restrict the request with `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs`, or use the two-step workflow.
- `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs` limits the request to specific shipping label partner accounts, and every rate in the response includes its `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID`. An unknown ID returns 400 ("ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID N does not exist."). Partners that do not apply to the order are always excluded: Amazon shipping for non-Amazon orders and Walmart shipping for non-Walmart orders. When omitted, rates are requested from all remaining active shipping partners.
- `ApplyDeliverByDate: true` returns only rates that deliver on or before `DeliverByDateUtc`. If `DeliverByDateUtc` is omitted, the delivery-by date of the order is used; if neither is available the request fails with 400.
- Success returns 200 multipart/mixed: the rates part, plus label and fulfillment parts when a label is purchased or matched.

See the Shipping Labels guide for the full one-step and two-step workflows.

LabelFormat.description: The format of the shipping label. Only `PDF` and `ZPL` are supported. Defaults to `PDF`.

200.description: Rates were returned. The body is multipart/mixed: a rates part, plus label and fulfillment parts when a label is purchased or matched.

post.description:
The Order Item Substitution feature allows sellers to replace ordered items with alternative products when the original items are unavailable, discontinued, or need to be swapped for business reasons. This is particularly useful for managing inventory shortages and maintaining customer satisfaction by providing suitable alternatives.

## Key Capabilities

### Business Use Cases
- **Out of Stock Management**: Replace unavailable items with similar products that are in stock
- **Product Discontinuation**: Substitute discontinued items with current alternatives
- **Quality Control**: Replace items that don't meet quality standards
- **Upgraded Substitutions**: Provide better alternatives at the same or lower price
- **Size/Color Variations**: Replace items when specific variants are unavailable

### Technical Features
- **Flexible Item Identification**: Identify items to substitute using either OrderItemID or SKU
- **Partial Quantity Substitution**: Substitute a portion of an item's quantity while keeping the remainder
- **Multiple Replacement Items**: Replace a single item with multiple different products
- **Custom Pricing**: Specify custom pricing for replacement items (UnitPrice, TaxPrice, ShippingPrice, etc.)
- **Shipping Override Control**: Control fulfillment details including distribution center, carrier, class, and tracking information
- **Bundle Support**: Substitute both individual items and bundle products
- **Partial Shipment Handling**: Substitute only unshipped quantities when items have been partially fulfilled

## Important Considerations

### Marketplace Support
Order item substitution is **not supported** for all marketplaces. Currently, substitutions are only available for:
- **Checkout Direct Orders** (orders created through the API)
- **Select Marketplace Orders** (contact Rithum for Brands support to confirm marketplace compatibility)

Attempting to substitute items from unsupported marketplaces will result in an error indicating that "Substitutions are not supported for this Marketplace."

### Order State Requirements
- Items must **not be fully shipped** to be eligible for substitution
- If an item has been partially shipped, only the unshipped quantity can be substituted
- Attempting to substitute a fully shipped item will result in an error

### Item Identification
- **OrderItemID**: Recommended for precise targeting of specific order items
- **SKU**: Can be used when SKU is unique within the order. If multiple items have the same SKU, the request will fail with an error suggesting the use of OrderItemID

### Pricing Behavior
- **UnitPrice**: Required for each replacement item
- **TaxPrice, ShippingPrice, ShippingTaxPrice, RecyclingFee**: Optional - will default to 0 if not specified
- Replacement item pricing is independent of the original item's pricing

### Shipping Overrides
- **Optional**: If not specified, the system will use default distribution center selection logic
- **DistributionCenterID**: Required if using shipping overrides
- **Quantity**: The quantity in shipping overrides must not exceed the replacement item's total quantity
- **Multiple Replacements**: Each replacement item can have its own shipping override configuration

## Workflow

1. **Identify the Order**: Specify the Order ID in the request URI: `POST v1/Orders({OrderID})/SubstituteItems`
2. **Specify Original Item**: Identify the item to substitute using either `OrderItemID` or `Sku` in the `OriginalItem` object
3. **Define Replacement Items**: Provide at least one replacement item with required pricing information
4. **Configure Shipping** (Optional): Add `ShippingOverrides` to control fulfillment details
5. **Submit Request**: The API will validate the request and process the substitution
6. **Verify Results**: Check the order to confirm the original item has been replaced with the new item(s)

## Validation Rules

The API performs the following validations:
- At least one substitution must be specified in the request
- Either `OrderItemID` or `Sku` must be specified for the original item
- Each replacement item must have either `ProductID` or `Sku` specified
- Replacement item `Quantity` must be greater than 0
- `UnitPrice` is required for each replacement item
- Original item must exist in the order and must not be fully shipped
- If using SKU to identify the original item, it must match exactly one item in the order
- If using shipping overrides, `DistributionCenterID` must be valid and accessible
- Shipping override quantities must not exceed replacement item quantities
- The order must be from a supported marketplace or be a Checkout Direct order

## Response Codes

- **204 No Content**: Substitution completed successfully
- **400 Bad Request**: Validation error (check error message for details)
- **401 Unauthorized**: Missing or invalid authentication token
- **404 Not Found**: Order not found or original item not found
- **500 Internal Server Error**: System error occurred (contact Rithum for Brands support)

## Examples

See the examples in the API documentation for common substitution scenarios including:
- Basic item substitution using SKU
- Partial quantity substitution
- Multiple replacement items
- Substitution with shipping overrides

ProductUploadArchiveDownload.description:
A resolved product upload archive and a short-lived, pre-signed URL for its bytes.
            
             The URL is a plain AWS SigV4 link straight to S3: no Complete session, no cookie and no
             handler in the path, so an unattended service can fetch it with nothing but an HTTP client.
             The bytes never pass through this API; it answers only what exists and where.

LabelName.description: Inventory label name. Joins to Product.Labels[] on the public REST surface.

LabelId.description:
Identifier of the label. Retained alongside {ChannelAdvisor.RestApi.Common.LabelTargeting.Models.LabelChannelTargetingItem.LabelName} so a consumer can
            still correlate rows when a label has been renamed or its name could not be resolved.

SiteAccountId.description:
Integer customer channel identifier of the targeted connection. This is the same
            identity the public REST surface calls SiteAccount / siteAccountId,
            and it is what distinguishes two connections to the same marketplace.

SiteId.description: Marketplace site identifier of the connection.

SiteName.description: Marketplace name of the connection (for example Amazon, eBay).

SiteAccountName.description:
Display name of the connection. The seller's custom name when one is set, otherwise
            the derived nickname, which appends the site instance for marketplaces that allow
            several accounts so same-marketplace connections remain distinguishable.

LabelChannelTargetingItem.description:
One edge in a profile's effective label-to-connection targeting: the label
             {ChannelAdvisor.RestApi.Common.LabelTargeting.Models.LabelChannelTargetingItem.LabelName} routes items to the channel connection identified by
             {ChannelAdvisor.RestApi.Common.LabelTargeting.Models.LabelChannelTargetingItem.SiteAccountId}.
            
             A connection may appear on several rows when more than one label routes to it
             (for example a Marketplaces connection with several active feeds, or a
             ChannelSync connection carrying both a primary and a Digital Marketing feed).
             A label may likewise appear on several rows when it routes to more than one
             connection. Consumers group by whichever key they need.

SiteAccountId.description:
Integer customer channel identifier of the connection the row belongs to. This is the same
            identity the public REST surface calls SiteAccount / siteAccountId, and it is
            what distinguishes two connections to the same marketplace.

SiteId.description:
Marketplace site identifier of the connection. Also the site whose enabled distribution
            centres produced this row, so two connections on the same site report the same centres.

SiteName.description: Marketplace name of the connection (for example Walmart, Target).

SiteAccountName.description:
Display name of the connection. The seller's custom name when one is set, otherwise the
            derived nickname, which appends the site instance for marketplaces that allow several
            accounts so same-marketplace connections remain distinguishable.

DistributionCenterId.description:
ChannelAdvisor distribution centre identifier — the client-level ClientDistCtrID.
            Joins to the DistributionCenters entity set and to the per-centre quantities a
            consumer reads from DCQuantity.

DistributionCenterCode.description:
Code of the ChannelAdvisor distribution centre, resolved from the centre itself rather than
             read from the stored mapping. Neither storage shape persists it: the shared shape keeps only
             the identifier, and the 1P shape keeps a name. Resolving it makes the field populated
             identically for every channel family instead of only for some.
            
             null when the identifier does not resolve to a distribution centre on the client.
             Soft-deleted centres do resolve, since one can still hold a site-priority record.

DistributionCenterPriority.description:
Order the site publishes this distribution centre in, from the site's distribution centre
             priority configuration. Lower is higher priority.
            
             Always present: every row originates from a priority record, which is what makes this
             non-nullable while the site-side fields below are not.

SiteDistributionCenterCode.description:
The marketplace's own identifier for the warehouse this distribution centre publishes to —
             a Walmart ship node, a Target warehouse code, a 1P warehouse code.
            
             null when the connection has no stored mapping for this centre, which is a normal
             state and means quantity is not routed anywhere for it. Never an empty string, including
             when the channel stored a blank one.

SiteDistributionCenterName.description:
The marketplace's own name for that warehouse. null when there is no stored mapping,
            and also when the mapping supplies no name — the common case, since most channels store a
            code and no name. Distinguishing null from "" matters here: the first says the
            channel gave us no name, the second would be indistinguishable from a channel that gave us
            a blank one.

DcMappingItem.description: One distribution centre a connection publishes quantity from, and the marketplace warehouse that quantity is routed to when a mapping has been configured. A row exists because the distribution centre is enabled for the connection's site, not because a mapping was stored for it. The stored mapping is a left join onto that set: {ChannelAdvisor.RestApi.Common.DcMappings.Models.DcMappingItem.SiteDistributionCenterCode} and {ChannelAdvisor.RestApi.Common.DcMappings.Models.DcMappingItem.SiteDistributionCenterName} are populated when one matches and null when none does. That mirrors what ChannelSync does at publish time, which iterates the site's enabled centres and enriches from the stored mapping — so an enabled centre with no mapping is visible as the routing gap it is, rather than being invisible. The consequence in the other direction: a stored mapping for a centre the site has not enabled produces no row, because the sync would not publish it either. The relation is many-to-many, so the shape is a flat edge list rather than a connection holding an array. A connection appears once per enabled centre, and a centre appears once per connection whose site enables it. Consumers group by whichever key they need.

Indicates the shipping state of an order.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Unshipped` | Fulfillment is incomplete. This is the default value. |
| `Shipped` | Fulfillment is complete. |
| `PartiallyShipped` | Fulfillment is incomplete. |
| `PendingShipment` | Fulfillment is incomplete. |
| `Canceled` | Fulfillment is complete. |
| `ThirdPartyManaged` | Fulfillment is complete. |

Webhook.DeliveryStatus.description:
Indicates the delivery state of a fulfillment.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `NoChange` | The fulfillment is unshipped. Making a request with this value will set a fulfillment or order to unshipped. |
| `InTransit` | The fulfillment is in transit to a location where the recipient may pick it up. Used for eBay In-Store-Pickup orders. |
| `ReadyForPickup` | The fulfillment has arrived at the pickup location and is ready for the recipient to pick up. Used for eBay In-Store-Pickup orders. |
| `Complete` | The fulfillment is complete and/or fully shipped. |
| `Canceled` | The items on this fulfillment have been canceled and will not be fulfilled. |
| `ThirdPartyManaged` | The fulfillment is handled outside Rithum. |
| `Confirmed` | The fulfillment location confirms receipt of the order. |
| `PickAndPack` | The items in the fulfillment are in the process of being retrieved and packed. |
| `LabelCreated` | The items in the fulfillment are packed and a label has been generated for pickup or retrieval. |
| `Held` | The fulfillment is in Held status when decisions are needed for change in the fulfillment. |
| `Delivered` | The shipment was delivered to the final destination. |
| `FailedDelivery` | The shipment failed delivery to the final destination. |

This document provides a high-level introduction to integrating with the Rithum For Brands API. It covers typical integration patterns, core components, environment setup, and frequently asked questions to help developers and partners get started quickly. --- ## Typical Integration Workflow A standard integration between a client system (your application) and Rithum For Brands involves: 1. **Sending product data** to Rithum For Brands (inventory creation and updates) 2. **Retrieving 'Ready To Ship' orders** from Rithum For Brands 3. **Sending shipping confirmations** back to Rithum For Brands 4. **Handling cancellations and refunds** as needed --- ## Core Integration Components ### Products - **Creating Products:** Add new products to Rithum For Brands, either individually or in batches. - **Updating Products:** Update product price, quantity, and attributes as needed. Prefer incremental updates for efficiency. - **Performance Note:** For catalogs over 20,000 products, consider using FTP for updates instead of the API. Contact Support for FTP setup. ### Orders - **Getting New Orders:** Retrieve only valid orders for fulfillment (not previously acknowledged, payment status Cleared). - **Acknowledging Orders:** Mark orders as exported after saving to your system to avoid duplicate retrievals. - **Shipping Orders:** Notify Rithum For Brands when orders are shipped; details are sent to the marketplace. - **Canceling/Refunding Orders:** Submit cancellation or refund requests; Rithum For Brands processes these with the marketplace. --- ## API Environment & Behavior - All client interactions use the same API endpoints for both live and test (sandbox) operations. - There is **no separate sandbox base URL**; production and sandbox accounts use the same endpoints. - Authorization and access procedures are identical across environments. ### Best Practice: Separate Authorizations - Use distinct API authorizations for production and sandbox posting accounts to keep environments separate. ### Posting Accounts - **Production Posting Account:** Used for live operations. - **Sandbox (Test) Posting Account:** Used for testing; recommended to include "Sandbox" or "Test" in the account name. Test accounts are not connected to marketplaces and are billable. - To request a test account, see the Knowledge Center article "Add a new posting account" (login required). --- ## Getting Started & FAQ ### Developer Access - Read and understand the [Terms of Use](#tag/Terms), then click on the requesting a developer account link below. After the account is granted, the email used to for the request is delivered an email with credentials. - Register for the Developer Network by [requesting a developer account](https://complete.channeladvisor.com/DeveloperNetwork/RequestApiDevKey.aspx) (external link). - API credentials require a Rithum For Brands customer to grant access to their account. ### Test Accounts - Test accounts are available for clients only and are billable. - Developers working for a client should have the client request a test account. ### REST API vs. SOAP API - The SOAP API is in maintenance mode; new integrations should use the REST API. - See the Knowledge Center for a comparison table and API request limits. ### Common Questions (FAQ)
How do I delete SKUs via the API?
Yes, you can delete SKUs using the DELETE Products request.
Can I archive SKUs via REST?
Not yet. This feature is coming soon.
What are the available scopes for REST?
See Introduction to OAuth 2.0 for available authorization scopes. Multiple scopes can be requested by separating them with spaces (e.g., orders inventory).
Are requests case sensitive?
- URLs before the ? are case-sensitive; after ? are not.
- JSON property names and enum values are case-sensitive.
Is there an authorization flow that doesn't require a Redirect URI?
Yes. Both the SOAP API Credentials Flow and Developer Console Token support authorization without a redirect URI.
Where can I find valid Site IDs and Site Names?
See the Knowledge Center for a list of valid Site IDs and Site Names.
Can I set the inventory quantity when creating a product?
No. Quantity updates must be made in a separate request after product creation.
Can I create attributes for a product during product creation?
Yes. Attributes can be created or updated in the same request as product creation.
Why don't new attributes or labels appear immediately in the web application?
It may take up to 30 minutes for new attributes or labels to appear in the web application.
Can I use SKU instead of Product ID for inventory adjustments?
No. Product/inventory adjustments require the Product ID, not the SKU.
How do I access marketplace/channel seller identifiers?
Use the SiteAccountID from the SiteAccounts entity. See documentation for details.
Is a machine-readable API format available?
Only $metadata is available for the REST API.
Can I prevent my refund or cancellation request from notifying the marketplace?
Yes. Use the PreventSiteProcessing property in Orders or Order Items requests.
Can I prevent my shipment update from notifying the marketplace?
Yes. Use the PreventMarketplaceCommunication property on the /v1/Orders/Ship endpoint or as a query string parameter on the /v1/Fulfillments endpoint.
How do I identify orders I've already imported that have been updated recently?
Use LastUpdatedDateUtc with exported=true as a parameter.
What is the difference between a production and sandbox (test) account?
Both use the same API endpoints. Sandbox accounts are standard posting accounts used for testing and are not connected to marketplaces.
--- For more information, see the Knowledge Center, Developer Console, or contact Rithum For Brands Support.

# Listings Guide Describes how to manage marketplace listings, including retrieving listings by site account and handling listing errors. --- ## Overview Marketplace listings represent the products you have listed for sale on various channels (e.g., Amazon, eBay). The Listings API allows you to: - Retrieve listings by site account or product - View listing details and status - Handle and review listing errors --- ## Validation & Paging - `profileId` is required if the integration has access to multiple profiles. If omitted and multiple profiles are available, a 400 error is returned. - `page` must be a positive integer (default: 1). A 400 error is returned if not. - `pageSize` must be between 1 and 100 (default: 100). A 400 error is returned if not. --- ## Endpoints & Example Responses ### Get Listings by Site Account Retrieve all marketplace listings for a specific site account. ```http GET /v1/listings/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 123, "SiteAccountID": 456, "ItemID": 789, "MarketplaceID": "AMZ", "Price": 19.99, "PriceLeader": "AMZ", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Electronics", "Quantity": 10, "ListingStatus": "Listed", "SyncStatus": "Synced", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-02T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 75.5, "Product": { "Sku": "ABC123", "Name": "Sample Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/siteaccount/456?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listings by Product Retrieve listings for a specific product. ```http GET /v1/listings/productid/{productId}?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 124, "SiteAccountID": 457, "ItemID": 54321, "MarketplaceID": "EBY", "Price": 29.99, "PriceLeader": "EBY", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Books", "Quantity": 5, "ListingStatus": "Listed", "SyncStatus": "Synced", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-03T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-04T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 60.0, "Product": { "Sku": "XYZ789", "Name": "Another Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/productid/54321?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listings by Site Account and Product Retrieve listings for a specific site account and product. ```http GET /v1/listings/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/productid/{productId}?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 125, "SiteAccountID": 456, "ItemID": 54321, "MarketplaceID": "AMZ", "Price": 24.99, "PriceLeader": "AMZ", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Electronics", "Quantity": 2, "ListingStatus": "Listed", "SyncStatus": "Synced", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-05T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-06T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 80.0, "Product": { "Sku": "XYZ789", "Name": "Another Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/siteaccount/456/productid/54321?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listing Errors by Site Account Retrieve listings with errors for a specific site account. ```http GET /v1/listings/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/errors?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 123, "SiteAccountID": 456, "ItemID": 789, "MarketplaceID": "AMZ", "Price": 19.99, "PriceLeader": "AMZ", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Electronics", "Quantity": 10, "ListingStatus": "Error", "SyncStatus": "Failed", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-02T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 75.5, "EstimatedPotentialRevenue": 199.90, "Severity": "Error", "ErrorMessage": "Invalid price", "ErrorCode": "ERR001", "ErrorTitle": "Price Error", "ErrorDetails": "The price is below the minimum allowed.", "Product": { "Sku": "ABC123", "Name": "Sample Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/siteaccount/456/errors?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listing Errors by Product Retrieve listings with errors for a specific product. ```http GET /v1/listings/productid/{productId}/errors?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 124, "SiteAccountID": 457, "ItemID": 54321, "MarketplaceID": "EBY", "Price": 29.99, "PriceLeader": "EBY", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Books", "Quantity": 5, "ListingStatus": "Error", "SyncStatus": "Failed", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-03T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-04T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 60.0, "EstimatedPotentialRevenue": 149.95, "Severity": "Error", "ErrorMessage": "Out of stock", "ErrorCode": "ERR002", "ErrorTitle": "Stock Error", "ErrorDetails": "No inventory available.", "Product": { "Sku": "XYZ789", "Name": "Another Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/productid/54321/errors?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listing Errors by Site Account and Product Retrieve listings with errors for a specific site account and product. ```http GET /v1/listings/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/productid/{productId}/errors?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 125, "SiteAccountID": 456, "ItemID": 54321, "MarketplaceID": "AMZ", "Price": 24.99, "PriceLeader": "AMZ", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Electronics", "Quantity": 2, "ListingStatus": "Error", "SyncStatus": "Failed", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-05T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-06T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 80.0, "EstimatedPotentialRevenue": 49.98, "Severity": "Error", "ErrorMessage": "Invalid SKU", "ErrorCode": "ERR003", "ErrorTitle": "SKU Error", "ErrorDetails": "The SKU does not exist.", "Product": { "Sku": "XYZ789", "Name": "Another Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listings/siteaccount/456/productid/54321/errors?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listing Error Rollups by Site Account Retrieve error rollups for a site account. ```http GET /v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ```
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ID": "rollup1", "SiteAccountID": 456, "Severity": "Error", "Message": "Multiple errors found.", "TotalListed": 5, "TotalNotListed": 2, "TotalErrorCount": 3, "Quantity": 7, "TotalEstimatedPotentialRevenue": 299.85, "Metadata": { "listedUrl": "/v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/456/rollup1/listed", "notListedUrl": "/v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/456/rollup1/notlisted", "errorsUrl": "/v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/456/rollup1/errors" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/456?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ### Get Listing Errors by Rollup (Errors, Listed, Not Listed) Retrieve listings with errors for a rollup: ```http GET /v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/{errorRollupId}/errors?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} GET /v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/{errorRollupId}/listed?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} GET /v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/{siteAccountId}/{errorRollupId}/notlisted?profileid={profileId}&page={page}&pagesize={pageSize} ``` - `errorRollupId` must be a valid rollup ID from the rollup endpoint above.
Example Response ```json { "items": [ { "ListingID": 126, "SiteAccountID": 456, "ItemID": 54322, "MarketplaceID": "AMZ", "Price": 34.99, "PriceLeader": "AMZ", "PriceSource": "Marketplace", "Category": "Electronics", "Quantity": 1, "ListingStatus": "Error", "SyncStatus": "Failed", "LastSubmittedDateUTC": "2023-01-07T12:00:00Z", "LastUpdateDateUTC": "2023-01-08T12:00:00Z", "BuyBoxPercentage": 90.0, "EstimatedPotentialRevenue": 34.99, "Severity": "Error", "ErrorMessage": "Marketplace restriction", "ErrorCode": "ERR004", "ErrorTitle": "Restriction Error", "ErrorDetails": "Listing restricted by marketplace.", "Product": { "Sku": "LMN456", "Name": "Restricted Product" } } ], "metadata": { "nextPageUrl": "/v1/listingserrorsrollup/siteaccount/456/rollup1/errors?page=2&pagesize=100" } } ```
--- ## Error Handling Standard API error codes apply: - `400 Bad Request` - malformed input, missing/invalid profileId, invalid page or pageSize - `401 Unauthorized` - invalid or expired token - `403 Forbidden` - insufficient scope or profile disabled - `404 Not Found` - resource not found - `429 Too Many Requests` - rate limit exceeded Inspect the response body for fields like `errorCode`, `message`, and `details`. --- ## Additional Resources - [Products & Inventory Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Products-and-Inventory-Guide) - [Orders Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Orders-Guide) - [Release Notes](apidocs#tag/Releases) # Webhooks Guide Learn how to configure, manage, and consume webhooks for real-time event notifications. --- ## What is a Webhook? A webhook is a method of communication between two systems using callbacks. Webhooks are triggered by an event in the source system (Rithum), which results in the source system requesting the configured Webhook URL where a payload for the event is posted. Webhooks use OAuth 2.0 for REST API Authorization to create an integration in which the client and account(s)/profile(s) are defined. In this integration, the Webhook event(s) subscription is created/configured. **Example:** A Webhook subscription is created for New Cleared Payment Orders in "My Profile - United States" and will be delivered to the configured HTTPS URL hosted by the client server. When an order changes to "Cleared" Payment Status in the web application, the Webhook subscription posts the order payload to the registered URL. --- ## Why Use Webhooks? - Orders are created frequently from various channel sources. - APIs require continuous polling to locate new orders. - With a webhook event for newly created orders, you are notified immediately and receive the complete payload. --- ## Use Cases Webhooks use cases include, but are not limited to: - Importing new data from Rithum into internal systems - Taking updated data from Rithum into internal systems - Notifying team members, partners, and systems about relevant data (orders, fulfillment, accounting, analytics, marketing) - Collecting data for long-term storage --- ## Steps to Receive Webhooks **Prerequisites:** - Developer Key - Client Profile Access with admin user credentials **Steps:** 1. Identify events to monitor and the event payloads to parse. 2. Create a webhook endpoint as an HTTP endpoint (URL) on your local server. 3. Test your webhook endpoint to ensure it works properly. 4. Deploy your webhook endpoint as a publicly accessible HTTPS URL. 5. Create webhook configuration, including the webhook HTTPS URL, in the Developer Console. 6. Accept requests from Rithum by returning 2xx response status codes and validate Rithum as source and payload creator. 7. Parse each event object. 8. Distribute parsed data to your systems. --- ## How Webhooks Work - A webhook is configured based on the existence of an event, and a delivery endpoint (webhook URI) is defined as part of the configuration. - One or more conditions can exist to trigger an event. When triggered, the source system initiates a POST request to deliver a payload to the delivery endpoint defined. - At the delivery endpoint, systems consume each payload at a rate conducive to their unique conditions. Client code should parse the payload data and distribute it as needed. - Optionally, payload IDs can be used to make requests against the ChannelAdvisor REST API without additional authorizations. --- ## Webhooks API Endpoints The following endpoints are available in the WebhooksController: - `GET /v1/Webhooks` - Retrieve all webhook subscriptions. - `GET /v1/Webhooks({id})` - Retrieve a specific webhook subscription by ID. - `POST /v1/Webhooks` - Create a new webhook subscription. - `PATCH /v1/Webhooks({id})` - Update an existing webhook subscription (partial update). - `PUT /v1/Webhooks({id})` - Update an existing webhook subscription (full update). - `DELETE /v1/Webhooks({id})` - Delete a webhook subscription. - `GET /v1/Webhooks({id})/RetrieveFailedEvents` - Start or check status of a job to retrieve failed webhook events. - `POST /v1/Webhooks({id})/RetryFailedEvents` - Retry delivery of failed webhook events for a given job token. - `POST /v1/Webhooks({id})/NewSigningSecret` - Expire the current signing secret and generate a new one. - `POST /v1/Webhooks({id})/UpdateAuthentication` - Update authentication settings for a webhook subscription. Below, the supported authentication methods for webhooks. | Type | Description | |-----------------------|--------------------| | **Signature Header** | *Always supplied as a header*.
Rithum signs webhook events via a Signature header so you can verify Rithum is sending the request and created the payload. This includes a timestamp and two base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 headers, generated from the webhook's Signing Secret. | | **Basic Authorization** | *Optional to enable*.
Rithum RFC2045-MIME (base-64) encodes a Username and Password value you configure and supplies it with an Authorization header in the webhook response. This allows you to quickly validate Rithum sent the request. | | **Custom Header** | *Optional to enable*.
Rithum supplies the header name and value you configure, and supplies them back as the header and value in the webhook response. This allows you to quickly validate Rithum sent the request. | Refer to the API reference for details on request/response payloads and required parameters. --- ## Example Payloads for POST, PATCH, and PUT Endpoints ### Create a Webhook (POST `/v1/Webhooks`) ```json { "Name": "Order Cleared Webhook", "Status": "Enabled", "WebhookUri": "https://yourserver.com/webhook-endpoint", "EventTypes": ["PaymentCleared", "SellerFulfillmentStatusChanged"], "AuthenticationType": "SigningSecret" } ``` - Do not include `ID` or `SigningSecret` when creating. - `WebhookUri` must be HTTPS. - `EventTypes` must not be empty. - `Status` must be "Enabled" or "Disabled". - For `SigningSecret`, do not supply any other authentication fields. #### Custom Header Authentication Example ```json { "Name": "Order Cleared Webhook", "Status": "Enabled", "WebhookUri": "https://yourserver.com/webhook-endpoint", "EventTypes": ["PaymentCleared"], "AuthenticationType": "CustomHeader", "CustomHeader": "X-Webhook-Auth", "CustomHeaderValue": "secret-value" } ``` - Both `CustomHeader` and `CustomHeaderValue` must be supplied. - Do not supply `BasicAuthUsername` or `BasicAuthPassword`. #### Basic Auth Authentication Example ```json { "Name": "Order Cleared Webhook", "Status": "Enabled", "WebhookUri": "https://yourserver.com/webhook-endpoint", "EventTypes": ["PaymentCleared"], "AuthenticationType": "BasicAuth", "BasicAuthUsername": "user", "BasicAuthPassword": "password" } ``` - Both `BasicAuthUsername` and `BasicAuthPassword` must be supplied. - Do not supply `CustomHeader` or `CustomHeaderValue`. ### Update a Webhook (PATCH `/v1/Webhooks({id})`) ```json { "Status": "Disabled", "WebhookUri": "https://yourserver.com/new-webhook-endpoint" } ``` - Only include fields you want to update. - Do not include `ID`, `SigningSecret`, or `AuthenticationType`. ### Update a Webhook (PUT `/v1/Webhooks({id})`) ```json { "Name": "Order Cleared Webhook", "Status": "Enabled", "WebhookUri": "https://yourserver.com/webhook-endpoint", "EventTypes": ["PaymentCleared", "SellerFulfillmentStatusChanged"], "CustomHeader": "", "CustomHeaderValue": "", "BasicAuthUsername": "", "BasicAuthPassword": "" } ``` - All required fields should be provided, similar to POST. - Do not include `ID`, `SigningSecret`, or `AuthenticationType`. - For authentication, follow the same rules as POST above. ### Retry Failed Events (POST `/v1/Webhooks({id})/RetryFailedEvents`) ```json { "Token": "abc123-def456" } ``` - `Token` is required and must be valid for the job. ### Generate New Signing Secret (POST `/v1/Webhooks({id})/NewSigningSecret`) - No payload required. ### Update Authentication (POST `/v1/Webhooks({id})/UpdateAuthentication`) #### SigningSecret Example ```json { "Value": { "AuthenticationType": "SigningSecret" } } ``` - Do not supply any other authentication fields. #### CustomHeader Example ```json { "Value": { "AuthenticationType": "CustomHeader", "CustomHeader": "X-Webhook-Auth", "CustomHeaderValue": "secret-value" } } ``` - Both `CustomHeader` and `CustomHeaderValue` must be supplied. - Do not supply `BasicAuthUsername` or `BasicAuthPassword`. #### BasicAuth Example ```json { "Value": { "AuthenticationType": "BasicAuth", "BasicAuthUsername": "user", "BasicAuthPassword": "password" } } ``` - Both `BasicAuthUsername` and `BasicAuthPassword` must be supplied. - Do not supply `CustomHeader` or `CustomHeaderValue`. --- ## Authentication Validation Rules - `AuthenticationType` must not be `Unknown`. - If `SigningSecret` is used, do not supply any other authentication fields. - If `CustomHeader` is used, both `CustomHeader` and `CustomHeaderValue` must be supplied, and do not supply basic auth fields. - If `BasicAuth` is used, both `BasicAuthUsername` and `BasicAuthPassword` must be supplied, and do not supply custom header fields. --- ## Error Handling Standard API error codes apply: - `400 Bad Request` - malformed input - `401 Unauthorized` - invalid or expired token - `403 Forbidden` - insufficient scope or profile disabled - `404 Not Found` - resource not found - `429 Too Many Requests` - rate limit exceeded Inspect the response body for fields like `errorCode`, `message`, and `details`. --- ## Webhook Event Payloads All webhook events follow a standard envelope structure containing metadata and a typed payload. The payload structure varies by event type (Order, Fulfillment, Adjustment). ### Event Envelope Every webhook POST request contains the following envelope: | Property | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `schema` | string | Event schema identifier (e.g., "/v1/orders/paymentcleared") | | `eventDateUtc` | string (ISO 8601) | Event timestamp in UTC | | `webhookId` | integer | The webhook subscription ID that triggered this event | | `payload` | object | Event-specific payload (see below) | **Example Envelope:** ```json { "schema": "/v1/orders/paymentcleared", "eventDateUtc": "2024-03-15T14:30:45.1234567Z", "webhookId": 12345, "payload": { ... } } ``` ### Event Types The API supports the following webhook event types: | Event Domain | Payload Type | Description | |---|---|---| | Orders | Order | Full order object including items, fulfillments, and adjustments | | Fulfillments | Fulfillment | Fulfillment details with order context (order items/fulfillments excluded) | | Adjustments | AdjustmentPayload | Order or item-level adjustment with order context (order custom fields excluded) | ### Supported Events The following webhook events are available. Use these event type names in the `EventTypes` field when creating or updating a webhook subscription. #### Order Events | Event Type | Trigger | Payload Type | |---|---|---| | `PaymentCleared` | Any order moves to `PaymentStatus = "Cleared"` from any source. | Order | | `SellerManagedPaymentCleared` | Orders with `DistributionCenterTypeRollup = "SellerManaged"` or `"Mixed"` move to `PaymentStatus = "Cleared"`. | Order | | `OrderModified` | An existing order, or any of its items or fulfillments, is modified after creation, from any source. | Order | **`PaymentCleared`** Fires when any order created in the platform — from any channel or source — reaches `PaymentStatus = "Cleared"`. Includes both seller-managed and externally-managed (FBA, WFS, ZFS) orders. Externally-managed orders may not yet have fulfillment/shipping data at time of event. An order that moves from `Cleared` back to `Pending Payment` and then to `Cleared` again will re-trigger this event. **`SellerManagedPaymentCleared`** Same trigger as `PaymentCleared` but limited to orders where `DistributionCenterTypeRollup = "SellerManaged"` or `"Mixed"`. Use this event to target seller-fulfillable orders. Orders with `"Mixed"` rollup may contain a combination of seller-managed and externally-managed fulfillments — identify and exclude external fulfillments by checking the distribution center type on each fulfillment. **`OrderModified`** Fires when an existing order — or any of its items or fulfillments — is modified after creation, from any source. The event envelope includes a top-level `changeReasons` string array indicating what changed; possible values are `ORDER_CHANGED`, `ITEM_CHANGED`, and `FULFILLMENT_CHANGED`. The `payload` contains the complete order object. --- #### Fulfillment Events | Event Type | Trigger | Payload Type | |---|---|---| | `SellerFulfillmentStatusChanged` | Seller-managed fulfillment `DeliveryStatus` changes to `"Complete"`. | Fulfillment | | `ExternalFulfillmentStatusChanged` | External fulfillment `ExternalFulfillmentStatus` changes to `"Complete"`, `"Failed"`, or `"Held"`. | Fulfillment | | `ExternallyManagedFulfillmentCompleted` | External fulfillment reaches completion with all status fields fully updated. | Fulfillment | **`SellerFulfillmentStatusChanged`** Fires when a seller-managed fulfillment's `DeliveryStatus` changes to `"Complete"`. Applies to distribution centers of type `Warehouse`, `DropShip`, or `RetailStore` (`DistributionCenterId >= 0`). A fulfillment can move in and out of `"Complete"` more than once; the event fires each time. Payload includes the triggering fulfillment, its items, and the order entity. `Order.ShippingStatus` indicates whether the overall order is `PendingShipment`, `PartiallyShipped`, or `Shipped`. **`ExternalFulfillmentStatusChanged`** Fires when an externally-managed fulfillment's `ExternalFulfillmentStatus` changes to `"Complete"`, `"Failed"`, or `"Held"`. Applies to external distribution centers (`DistributionCenterId < 0`) including Amazon FBA, Walmart Fulfillment Services (WFS), Zalando Fulfillment Services (ZFS), and Rithum Fulfillment Services (RFS) partners. `ExternalFulfillmentStatus` tracks communication to the external partner and cannot be set via API. The event fires each time the condition is met. **`ExternallyManagedFulfillmentCompleted`** *(Added May 2026)* Fires after an externally-managed fulfillment completes and all status fields — including `DeliveryStatus` and `Order.ShippingStatus` — are fully updated. Use this event instead of `ExternalFulfillmentStatusChanged` when your integration requires accurate delivery and shipping status at time of receipt. `ExternalFulfillmentStatusChanged` is preserved for backwards compatibility. --- #### Adjustment Events | Event Type | Trigger | Payload Type | |---|---|---| | `CancellationStarted` | Order-level or item-level cancellation adjustment is newly created from any source. | Adjustment | | `CancellationFinalized` | Order-level or item-level cancellation adjustment reaches a terminal status. | Adjustment | | `RefundStarted` | Order-level or item-level refund adjustment is newly created from any source. Includes Buyer Initiated Returns. | Adjustment | | `RefundFinalized` | Order-level or item-level refund adjustment reaches a terminal status. | Adjustment | **`CancellationStarted`** Fires when a cancellation adjustment (`AdjustmentType = "Cancellation"`) is newly created for an order or item from any source (web application, API, channel). Check `CreatedSource` in the payload to filter by relevant sources. Buyer Initiated Returns do not generate cancellation events — returns are only possible on shipped products and appear as refund events. **`CancellationFinalized`** Fires when a cancellation adjustment reaches a terminal `AdjustmentStatus`: `PostProcessingComplete`, `Error`, `InformationOnly`, or `RejectionCompleted`. Check `LastUpdatedSource` in the payload to identify the finalizing source. **`RefundStarted`** Fires when a refund adjustment (`AdjustmentType = "Refund"`) is newly created for an order or item from any source. Includes Buyer Initiated Returns — these will have `CreatedSource = "Channel"`. **`RefundFinalized`** Fires when a refund adjustment reaches a terminal `AdjustmentStatus`: `PostProcessingComplete`, `Error`, `InformationOnly`, or `RejectionCompleted`. Includes finalization of Buyer Initiated Returns. > **Adjustment payload note:** For all four adjustment events, the triggering `OrderAdjustment` or `OrderItemAdjustment` is surfaced at the top of the payload, followed by the complete order (including all other adjustments, fulfillments, and items). The triggering adjustment also appears nested within its parent item in the order payload. --- ### Order Events Order events contain the full order object with items, fulfillments, and adjustments. **Payload Structure:** - `Payload.Order` - Complete order object including items, fulfillments, adjustments, and order attributes **Example Payload:** ```json { "Payload": { "ID": 98765, "ProfileID": 12345, "SiteOrderID": "AMZ-123-4567890", "BuyerEmailAddress": "customer@example.com", "CreatedDateUtc": "2024-03-15T14:30:45.1234567Z", "TotalPrice": 149.9900, "Items": [...], "Fulfillments": [...], "Adjustments": [...] } } ``` **`OrderModified` envelope:** In addition to the standard order payload, `OrderModified` events include a top-level `changeReasons` string array on the event envelope indicating what changed. Possible values are `ORDER_CHANGED`, `ITEM_CHANGED`, and `FULFILLMENT_CHANGED`. ```json { "schema": "/v1/orders/ordermodified", "eventDateUtc": "2026-06-17T06:54:44.2553381Z", "webhookId": 12345, "payload": { ... }, "changeReasons": [ "ITEM_CHANGED", "ORDER_CHANGED", "FULFILLMENT_CHANGED" ] } ``` ### Fulfillment Events Fulfillment events contain the fulfillment details and a subset of the order (items excluded from order per serialization rules). **Payload Structure:** - `Payload.Fulfillment` - Fulfillment object with items - Order object is included with CustomFields and OrderAttributes. Items, Fulfillments, and Adjustments are omitted. **Example Payload:** ```json { "Payload": { "ID": 55555, "OrderID": 98765, "ShippingCarrier": "UPS", "ShippingClass": "Ground", "TrackingNumber": "1Z999AA10123456784", "Items": [...] } } ``` ### Adjustment Events Adjustment events contain either an order-level or item-level adjustment, plus a subset of the order (CustomFields omitted). **Payload Structure:** - `Payload.OrderAdjustment` - Order-level adjustment (nullable, present if order-level adjustment) - `Payload.OrderItemAdjustment` - Item-level adjustment (nullable, present if item-level adjustment) - Order object is included with Items, Fulfillments, Adjustments, and OrderAttributes. CustomFields are omitted. **Example Payload (Order-Level Adjustment):** ```json { "Payload": { "OrderAdjustment": { "ID": 77777, "OrderID": 98765, "Reason": "CustomerReturn", "Amount": -10.0000, "RefundIssuedDateUtc": "2024-03-16T10:15:30.1234567Z" }, "OrderItemAdjustment": null, "Order": { "ID": 98765, "ProfileID": 12345, ... } } } ``` **Example Payload (Item-Level Adjustment):** ```json { "Payload": { "OrderAdjustment": null, "OrderItemAdjustment": { "ID": 88888, "OrderItemID": 111111, "OrderID": 98765, "Reason": "Damaged", "AdjustedQuantity": 1, "PerItemAdjustment": -69.9900, "TotalAdjustment": -69.9900 }, "Order": { "ID": 98765, "ProfileID": 12345, ... } } } ``` ### Data Types #### Decimals All decimal/monetary fields use fixed-point format with 4 decimal places: `149.9900` #### Enums Enum values are serialized as strings. For example, `AdjustmentReason` enum values like `CustomerReturn`, `Damaged`, etc. ### Schema References For complete schema definitions including all properties and types, see the generated OpenAPI specification under [components/schemas](#schema/Webhook.WebhookEventEnvelope) with `Webhook.` prefix: - `Webhook.WebhookEventEnvelope` - `Webhook.OrderEventPayload` - `Webhook.FulfillmentEventPayload` - `Webhook.AdjustmentEventPayload` - `Webhook.Order` - `Webhook.OrderItem` - `Webhook.Fulfillment` - `Webhook.FulfillmentItem` - `Webhook.OrderAdjustment` - `Webhook.OrderItemAdjustment` - And more... --- ## Additional Resources - [Authorization & Authentication Guide](#tag/Guides/API-Authentication-Guide) - [Release Notes](#tag/Releases) # Batch Requests Guide The `$batch` endpoint allows you to combine multiple API requests into a single HTTP request. This reduces the number of round trips to the server and can improve performance for integrations that need to make many related API calls. --- ## Background Batch processing under OData standards uses the `multipart/mixed` content type to bundle multiple operations into a single HTTP request. To understand the full specification, read [11.7 Batch Requests](https://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/odata/v4.01/odata-v4.01-part1-protocol.html#sec_BatchRequests) in the OData protocol documentation. > **Important:** It is recommended to batch no more than **100** requests at a time regardless of what action is being performed (`GET`, `PUT`, `POST`, etc.). If requests time out, scale back the number of requests being batched together. > **Important:** The batch request itself, as well as each individual request within the body of the batch, all count toward [rate limits](#tag/Guides/API-Rate-limiting-Guide). Batches are therefore more expensive than individual requests with regard to request limits. --- ## When to Use Batch Requests Batch requests are most useful when you need to: - **Perform multiple operations** in a single HTTP call (e.g., updating several products or retrieving multiple orders). - **Improve integration performance** by minimizing network overhead. --- ## Incompatible Endpoints There are two endpoints that are incompatible with batch requests and do not have alternate methods: - `POST /v1/Orders(ID)/Export` - `POST`, `PATCH`, or `PUT /v1/DistributionCenters(ID)/OperatingHours` ### Aliased Endpoints Requiring Alternate URIs Several aliased endpoints will not work in `$batch` requests. The real URI must be used instead: | Endpoint Not Supported in `$batch` | Real URI Supported in `$batch` | |-----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `PATCH` or `PUT /v1/Products(ID)/Attributes('AttributeName')` | `POST /v1/AttributeValues` to update a single attribute, or `POST /v1/Products(ID)/UpdateAttributes` to update single or multiple attributes, or `PATCH` or `PUT /v1/AttributeValues(ProductID=ID, Name='Attribute Name')` to update a single attribute | | `DELETE /v1/Products(ID)/Attributes('AttributeName')` | `DELETE /v1/AttributeValues(ProductID=ID, Name='Attribute Name')` | | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/Products(ID)/Images('PlacementName')` | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/Images(ProductID=ID, PlacementName='Placement Name')` | | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/Products(ID)/Labels('LabelName')` | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/ProductLabels(ProductID=ID, Name='Label Name')` | | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/Products(ID)/BundleComponents(ComponentID)` | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/ProductBundleComponents(ProductID=ID, ComponentID=Component ID)` | | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/Products(ID)/DCQuantities(DC Id)` | `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE /v1/DCQuantities(ProductID=ID, DistributionCenterID=DC ID)` | --- ## Request Format ### Resource URL ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/$batch ``` ### Required Headers | Header | Value | Required | Description | |----------------|------------------------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `Content-Type` | `multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset` | Yes | Defines the MIME content to be delivered. Since the content will vary by the requests included, this allows for multiple parts to be defined within the body. The value `changeset` is used as the batch delimiter within the body. This can be changed to any consistent value (without special characters or spaces) as long as the batch delimiters in the body are changed to match. | | `Authorization`| `Bearer {access_token}` | Yes | A valid OAuth 2.0 access token. | ### Request Body Structure The request body uses a multipart structure with batch and changeset delimiters. Each changeset represents an individual request within the batch. > **Note:** Line breaks within the body are critical for batch requests to execute properly. Ensure a newline is inserted where indicated. | Value | Required | Description | |----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `--batch` | Yes | Defines the beginning of the batch. | | `Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset` | Yes | Defines the batching MIME content. | | `--changeset` | Yes | Defines the first request within the batch. Repeat this between each request. If the header of the request defines something other than `boundary=changeset`, this value must match. | | `Content-Type: application/http` | Yes | Defines the batching MIME content for processing the request within the batch. This same format is used for every changeset in the batch request. | | `Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary` | Yes | Defines the transfer encoding to ensure the request is processed accurately. | | `Content-ID: {N}` | Yes | A numeric value representing the request being made. Use a simple integer in increasing value, not duplicated within the batch request. For example: `Content-ID: 1` is the first changeset, `Content-ID: 2` is the second, and so on. | | *(newline)* | Yes | Insert a newline here to ensure accurate processing. | | Method and URL | Yes | The full URL of the request as provided in an individual request format. Include any IDs or string values formatted properly. For example: `PUT https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/Fulfillments(11353895) HTTP/1.1` | | `Content-Type: application/json` | Conditional | Required if the request is a `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` and contains a body. | | *(newline)* | Yes | Insert a newline here to ensure accurate processing. | | Body content in JSON format | Conditional | Required if the request is a `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` and contains a body. Format and required properties will vary by the request being made. | | *(newline)* | Yes | Insert a newline here to ensure accurate processing. | | `--changeset--` | Yes | Defines the end of the changeset. | | `--batch--` | Yes | Defines the end of the batch. | --- ## Example: Update Quantity on Three Items The following example combines two quantity updates with a third quantity update, all using the `UpdateQuantity` action. ### Example Request ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/$batch Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset Authorization: Bearer {access_token} ``` ``` --batch Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=changeset --changeset Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary Content-ID: 1 POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/Products(25129205)/UpdateQuantity HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json { "Value": { "UpdateType": "UnShipped", "Updates": [ { "DistributionCenterID": 1, "Quantity": 71 } ] } } --changeset Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary Content-ID: 2 POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/Products(25129545)/UpdateQuantity HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json { "Value": { "UpdateType": "UnShipped", "Updates": [ { "DistributionCenterID": 1, "Quantity": 999 } ] } } --changeset Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary Content-ID: 3 POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/v1/Products(25139099)/UpdateQuantity HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json { "Value": { "UpdateType": "UnShipped", "Updates": [ { "DistributionCenterID": 1, "Quantity": 999 } ] } } --changeset-- --batch-- ``` ### Example Response (Success) ``` --batchresponse_bda71625-5372-40c7-9c61-a4d55c94f7d2 Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary HTTP/1.1 204 No Content --batchresponse_bda71625-5372-40c7-9c61-a4d55c94f7d2 Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary HTTP/1.1 204 No Content --batchresponse_bda71625-5372-40c7-9c61-a4d55c94f7d2 Content-Type: application/http Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary HTTP/1.1 204 No Content --batchresponse_bda71625-5372-40c7-9c61-a4d55c94f7d2-- ``` --- ## Error Handling - If the batch request itself is malformed, the server returns an appropriate HTTP error status (e.g., `400 Bad Request`). - Individual requests within a batch may succeed or fail independently. Always check the HTTP status line of each individual response part. - Verify that the `Content-ID` values in the response match the corresponding requests. --- ## Limits and Best Practices - **Maximum requests per batch:** It is recommended to batch no more than **100** requests at a time. If requests time out, scale back the number of requests being batched together. - **Rate limits:** The batch request itself and each individual operation within it are all counted against your [rate limits](#tag/Guides/API-Rate-limiting-Guide). Plan batch sizes accordingly. - **Line breaks:** Line breaks within the batch body are critical. Missing or extra line breaks will cause requests to fail. - **Content-ID:** Use unique, incrementing integer `Content-ID` values for each changeset to correctly identify responses. - **Boundary consistency:** If you customize the `boundary` value in the `Content-Type` header, ensure all delimiters in the body match. - **Incompatible endpoints:** Some endpoints are not compatible with `$batch`. See the [Incompatible Endpoints](#incompatible-endpoints) and [Aliased Endpoints](#aliased-endpoints-requiring-alternate-uris) sections above. # Orders Guide Learn how to retrieve, acknowledge, ship, cancel, and refund orders using the Orders API. --- ## Flow of Order Processing The Order and Fulfillment retrieval and update process usually flows like this with the REST API: 1. **Order is placed on a marketplace** 2. **Order is retrieved from the marketplace by Rithum** 3. **Rithum acknowledges and confirms receipt of the order as necessary within the time frame required by the marketplaces** - Orders are typically retrieved from marketplaces every 15 minutes. 4. **Client retrieves a group of orders that haven't already been imported into their system** - Refer to [Common order retrieval methods](apidocs#tag/Guides/Orders-Guide/Common-Order-Retrieval-Methods) for common filters. - For marketplace-specific examples, see [Marketplace-specific order responses](#marketplace-specific-order-responses). 5. **Client marks imported orders as Exported in the API** - Each order must be marked as exported individually. - See [Exported and non-exported orders overview](apidocs#tag/Guides/Orders-Guide/Exported-and-Non-Exported-Orders-Overview). > **Tip:** For most use cases, using a [webhook](apidocs#tag/Webhooks) to receive order notifications is more efficient and reliable than polling the Orders API. Webhooks provide real-time updates, reduce API traffic, and minimize latency, ensuring you receive new order information as soon as it is available. Polling, by contrast, can introduce delays and unnecessary load on both client and server. --- ## Common Order Retrieval Methods Retrieve non exported orders using filters and OData queries. Example: ```http GET /v1/Orders?$filter=PaymentStatus eq 'Cleared' and ShippingStatus eq 'Unshipped'&exported=false ``` Refer to API documentation for more filter options. --- ## Exported and Non-Exported Orders Overview After importing orders, mark them as exported: ```http POST /v1/Orders({orderId})/Exported ``` This prevents duplicate imports and helps track order processing status. --- ## Update an Order Update select fields on an existing order using PATCH. Only include fields you want to change. Endpoint - PATCH /v1/Orders({orderId}) Behavior - Returns 400 Bad Request if the body is empty (No changes specified). - Returns 404 Not Found if the order does not exist or you do not have access to its profile. - On success, returns 204 No Content. Example: Update SellerOrderID ```http PATCH /v1/Orders(12345678) Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json { "SellerOrderID": "SO-100045", } ``` Partial updates are supported. Only the provided properties are evaluated and applied. --- ## Shipments & Fulfillments Mark items or fulfillments as shipped and provide tracking info: ```http POST /v1/Orders({orderId})/Ship Content-Type: application/json { "TrackingNumber": "1Z999AA10123456784", "Carrier": "UPS", "Class": "Ground", "ShippedDate": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z", "Items": [ { "Sku": "ABC123", "Quantity": 1 } ] } ``` Partial shipments are supported. The API will create new fulfillments as needed. You can also retrieve fulfillments for an order: ```http GET /v1/Orders({orderId})/Fulfillments ``` Or retrieve a specific fulfillment: ```http GET /v1/Fulfillments({fulfillmentId}) ``` --- ## Cancellations and Refunds Overview - Not all marketplaces allow all types of refunds (e.g., partial quantity refunds may not be allowed). - Exchanges are not supported in Rithum or any marketplace. For exchanges, communicate directly with the buyer; do not send order adjustment information to Rithum or the marketplace. Cancel or refund orders/items by issuing adjustments: ```http POST /v1/Orders({orderId})/Adjust Content-Type: application/json { "Reason": "OutOfStock", "Items": [ { "Sku": "ABC123", "Quantity": 1 } ] } ``` You can also adjust a specific order item: ```http POST /v1/OrderItems({orderItemId})/Adjust Content-Type: application/json { "Reason": "BuyerRequest", "Quantity": 1 } ``` - Use different reasons for cancellations vs. refunds. The available reasons are marketplace-specific. To get the valid list of reasons for a specific marketplace, call the Sites API: ```http GET /v1/Sites ``` Example response (condensed): ```json [ { "ID": 123, "SiteName": "Example Marketplace", "AdjustmentReasons": [ { "Code": 1, "Description": "OutOfStock" }, { "Code": 2, "Description": "BuyerRequest" } ] } ] ``` Each site in the response will include an `AdjustmentReasons` property, which contains the valid codes and descriptions for cancellations and refunds for that marketplace. Use the appropriate code in the `Reason` field of your adjustment request. - The API determines the correct marketplace action based on shipped status and reason. - For refunds, the item must already be shipped. With Streams, you can retrieve actionable buyer-initiated returns (Return Merchandise Authorizations, RMAs) that hit specific actionable states: - **NewRma** - **ReadyForReturn** --- ## Authorization & Integration Scope - Streams return data for all profiles associated with an integration ("refresh token"). - For more information, see: - [Authorization types and Request Authorization methods](apidocs#tag/Guides/API-Authentication-Guide) - [Working with multiple accounts](apidocs#tag/Guides/Standard-Integration-Guide) --- ## Implementation Workflow 1. **Create a Stream for an event.** 2. **Retrieve Streams by StreamEventID**, identifying the last StreamEventID in the payload. 3. **Retrieve next set of Stream events** using the last StreamEventID + 1 as the start. - If events are available, you receive a `200 OK` with a body. - If no more events, you receive a `204 No Content`. 4. **Repeat** until no more StreamEvents are returned. 5. **Check for more StreamEvents every 5-10 minutes.** --- ## Creating a Stream To create a new stream, send a POST request to `/v1/Streams` with a JSON body specifying the event types and (optionally) the status.
