Types of Products A product in the platform can be one of the following types: | Type | Description | Buyable | Has Quantity | |------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------|--------------| | Standalone | The default type of product. Can be listed and purchased without impact to other products. May be a component in a Bundle. When component in a Bundle, quantity changes will impact available quantity in the Bundle. | Yes | Yes | | Parent | A container for one or more child items that vary by one or more attributes such as size or color. A parent does not have quantity and is not purchasable. | No | No | | Child | A child product can be purchased and is always related to a single parent product. A child product usually exists for each variation of a parent product. | Yes | Yes | | Bundle | Bundles are a virtual container for one or more other buyable items. For example, a bundle may contain one camera and two memory cards. Each bundle component, which can be either a standalone or child product, has a component multiplier quantity, which is used to calculate the bundle's overall quantity. | Yes | Yes (calculated) | --- ## Flow of Product Creation & Management The product creation and update process usually flows like this with the REST API: 1. **Provide new SKU data to the system as needed.** 2. **Ensure pre-requisites are in place:** - Variation names/types - Distribution Centers 3. **Create SKUs:** - Apply all known product attributes within the same product creation request for ease of use. - Otherwise, use individual attribute requests to append new attributes. 4. **Apply quantity information to products.** 5. **Once a product is created, you can:** - **CREATE Bundles:** Apply products to bundles for sale. - **UPDATE Field Data:** Adjust data for an existing product in an existing field. - **ADD More Data:** Add data for an existing product in an existing or new field. - **DELETE Individual Data:** Clear a data point, leaving it blank. - **DELETE the Entire Product:** Remove a product from the system if no longer active. - **UPLOAD Product Data:** Add or update data in bulk. - **EXPORT Product Data:** Extract data in bulk. --- ## Creating Products Create products using the API by sending a POST request with product details: ```http POST /v1/Products Content-Type: application/json { "Sku": "ABC123", "Name": "Camera", "Quantity": 10, "Attributes": [ { "Name": "Color", "Value": "Black" }, { "Name": "Size", "Value": "Medium" } ] } ``` - Include all relevant attributes and quantity information in the creation request. - For parent/child relationships, specify `IsParent`, `ParentProductID`, and `RelationshipName` as needed. --- ## Updating Products & Inventory Update product fields or inventory quantities: ```http PATCH /v1/Products({productId}) Content-Type: application/json { "Quantity": 15, "Attributes": [ { "Name": "Color", "Value": "Red" } ] } ``` - Use PATCH for partial updates. - To update attributes, send the full set of attributes or use attribute-specific endpoints. --- ## FTP Alternatives for Large Catalogs For catalogs over 20,000 products, consider using FTP for bulk updates and exports: - **FTP Upload:** Contact Support to set up FTP for product data uploads. - **FTP Export:** Use FTP to extract product data in bulk. - FTP is recommended for very large catalogs to avoid API rate limits and improve performance. --- ## Bundles Create bundles by specifying bundle components and their quantities: ```http POST /v1/Products Content-Type: application/json { "Sku": "BUNDLE001", "Name": "Camera Bundle", "BundleType": "BundleItem", "BundleComponents": [ { "ComponentSku": "CAM123", "Quantity": 1 }, { "ComponentSku": "MEM456", "Quantity": 2 } ] } ``` - Bundle quantity is calculated based on component quantities and multipliers. ### Assembly Bundles Assembly bundles require distribution centers to be assigned at creation time. Use `BundleType: "AssemblyBundleItem"` and supply `AssemblyBundleDistributionCenters` with a non-empty list of distribution center IDs: ```http POST /v1/Products Content-Type: application/json { "Title": "My Assembly Bundle", "BundleType": "AssemblyBundleItem", "AssemblyBundleDistributionCenters": [101, 102], "BundleComponents": [ { "ComponentSku": "CAM123", "Quantity": 1 }, { "ComponentSku": "MEM456", "Quantity": 2 } ] } ``` - `AssemblyBundleDistributionCenters` is **required and must be non-empty** when `BundleType` is `AssemblyBundleItem`. Supplying it with any other `BundleType` returns `400 Bad Request`. - To retrieve distribution center assignments on a product, use `$expand`: ``` GET /v1/Products(12345)?$expand=AssemblyBundleDistributionCenters ``` - Without `$expand`, the field is present in the response but returns an empty array. It is not available in list or filter endpoints (`GET /v1/Products?$filter=...`). --- ## Exporting Product Data Export product data in bulk using the Product Export API. This is ideal for extracting large sets of product data with advanced filtering and field selection. ### How It Works 1. **Request an export:** - Send a POST request to `/v1/ProductExport` with optional filters and a list of fields to export. - The export is queued and processed asynchronously. 2. **Check export status:** - Use the token returned from the export request to check the status and retrieve the download link. ### Export Limits - Maximum 10,000,000 products exported per day per account. - Maximum 10 export requests per minute per profile. - Single export files are limited to 5 GB. - Exports are processed in the order received. ### Requesting an Export **POST /v1/ProductExport** - Use the `$filter` query parameter to filter products (see table below for supported filters). - In the request body, provide a comma-separated list of field names to export (e.g., `SKU,Name,Quantity`). **Example:** ```http POST /v1/ProductExport?$filter=substringof(SKU, 'CAM') and TotalQuantity gt 0 Content-Type: text/plain SKU,Name,Quantity,CreateDateUtc ``` **Supported Filters:** | Filter | Operators | Example | |------------------------------------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------| | substringof(SKU, String) | N/A | substringof(SKU, 'value') | | startswith(SKU, String) | N/A | startswith(SKU, 'value') | | CreateDateUtc operator DateTime | lt, le, gt, ge | CreateDateUtc lt '3/31/2018 13:00:00' | | UpdateDateUtc operator DateTime | lt, le, gt, ge | UpdateDateUtc gt '9/1/2017 14:00:00' | | LastSaleDateUtc operator DateTime | lt, le, gt, ge | LastSaleDateUtc le '9/6/2017 15:00:00' | | ReceivedDateUtc operator DateTime | lt, le, gt, ge | ReceivedDateUtc ge '3/1/2018 16:00:00' | | ClassificationName operator String | eq | ClassificationName eq 'value' | | Labels operator String | eq | Labels eq 'value' | | TotalQuantity operator Integer | lt, le, gt, ge, eq | TotalQuantity ge 10 | | TotalAvailableQuantity operator Integer | lt, le, gt, ge, eq | TotalAvailableQuantity ge 10 | | PendingCheckoutQuantity operator Integer | lt, le, gt, ge, eq | PendingCheckoutQuantity ge 10 | | PendingPaymentQuantity operator Integer | lt, le, gt, ge, eq | PendingPaymentQuantity ge 10 | | PendingShipmentQuantity operator Integer | lt, le, gt, ge, eq | PendingShipmentQuantity ge 10 | **Sample Response:** ```json { "Token": "abc123xyz", "Status": "Queued" } ``` ### Checking Export Status and Downloading **GET /v1/ProductExport/CheckStatus?token={token}** - Use the token from the export request to check the status and get the download URL when ready. **Example:** ```http GET /v1/ProductExport/CheckStatus?token=abc123xyz ``` **Sample Response:** ```json { "Status": "Complete", "DownloadUrl": "https://.../exportfile.csv" } ``` ### Notes - For very large catalogs, FTP export is recommended. Contact Support to set up FTP access. - Exports are not immediate; processing time depends on catalog size and system load. - If you exceed rate or size limits, you will receive a 429 (Too Many Requests) response. --- ## Deleting Products & Data Delete individual data points or entire products: ```http DELETE /v1/Products({productId}) ``` - To clear a field, send an update with a blank value. - To remove a product, use the DELETE endpoint. --- ## Additional Resources - [Orders Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Orders-Guide) - [Release Notes](apidocs#tag/Releases) # API Authentication Guide This guide describes how to authenticate and authorize applications to the Rithum For Brands REST API using OAuth 2.0. It covers supported flows, token management, endpoints, scopes, request formats, and error handling. --- ## Integration Activity & Token Expiry - **Integrations are deactivated if unused for 30 days.** - **Refresh tokens expire 30 days after the last access token is generated.** - To keep integrations active, use the refresh token at least every 29 days. - If a refresh token expires, API requests will fail with an `invalid_grant` error. --- ## Prerequisites - Register your application in the [Developer Console](https://api.channeladvisor.com/developerconsole). - Obtain your Application ID and Shared Secret. - A Developer Key and Password are required to log in and register applications. --- ## Authorization Flows ### 1. OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow - **Recommended for web server applications.** - Most secure; supports refresh tokens and webhooks. - Requires user interaction to grant access. ### 2. Developer Console Token - **For automated or backend integrations.** - Allows manual creation of refresh tokens for use with the token endpoint. - Supports webhooks. ### 3. SOAP API Credentials Flow - **For existing SOAP API integrations.** - Allows migration to REST API using existing credentials. - Does **not** support refresh tokens or webhooks. --- ## Token Types & Lifecycles - **Access Token**: Required for all API requests. Expires in 1 hour. - **Refresh Token**: Used to obtain new access tokens. Expires after 30 days of inactivity or if access is revoked. --- ## Endpoints - `POST /oauth2/authorize` - Request user authorization - `POST /oauth2/token` - Exchange code or refresh token for access token - `GET /oauth2/identity` - Retrieve identity information - `POST /oauth2/revoke` - Revoke access/refresh tokens --- ## Authorization Scopes - `orders` - `orders.readonly` - `inventory` - `inventory.readonly` Combine multiple scopes by separating them with spaces (e.g., `orders inventory`). --- ## Requesting Authorization ### Authorization Code Flow 1. **Redirect user to authorize endpoint:** - `client_id`: Application ID - `response_type`: `code` - `scope`: Space-delimited list of scopes - `redirect_uri`: Must match the URI registered in Developer Console - `access_type`: `offline` (to receive a refresh token) Example: ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/authorize Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded Body: client_id=[application id]&response_type=code&access_type=offline&scope=orders inventory&redirect_uri=[redirect uri] ``` 2. **User grants access:** - Redirected to your `redirect_uri` with `code` parameter. 3. **Exchange code for tokens:** - POST to `/oauth2/token` with: - Header: `Authorization: Basic [base64(application id:shared secret)]` - Body: `grant_type=authorization_code&code=[authorization code]&redirect_uri=[redirect uri]` Example: ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic MTIzNDU6YWJjZGU= Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded Body: grant_type=authorization_code&code=[code]&redirect_uri=[redirect uri] ``` Response: ```json { "access_token": "...", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "..." } ``` ### Refreshing an Access Token - POST to `/oauth2/token` with: - Header: `Authorization: Basic [base64(application id:shared secret)]` - Body: `grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=[refresh token]` Example: ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic MTIzNDU6YWJjZGU= Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded Body: grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=[refresh token] ``` Response: ```json { "access_token": "...", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600 } ``` ### Implicit Flow - For client-side desktop, mobile, or JavaScript applications. - No shared secret required; does not return a refresh token. - Use anti-forgery tokens for security. Example: ```http GET https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=[application id]&response_type=token&scope=orders&redirect_uri=[redirect uri]&state=[anti-forgery token] ``` Redirect URI receives: ``` https://[redirect uri]?access_token=[access token]&token_type=Bearer&expires_in=3600&state=[anti-forgery token] ``` --- ## Token Usage in Requests - **Preferred:** HTTP header - `Authorization: Bearer [access token]` - **Alternative:** Query string parameter - `access_token=[access token]` --- ## Error Handling ### Common Error Responses - `invalid_client`: Invalid Application ID/Shared Secret or encoding. - `invalid_grant`: Expired or invalid refresh token. - `integration_revoked`: Authorization revoked by account admin. - `Authorization has been denied for this request.`: Expired or invalid access token. #### Example Error Response ```json { "error": "invalid_grant" } ``` --- ## Best Practices - Store refresh tokens securely; do not lose them. - Never embed shared secrets in client-side code. - Always use HTTPS for redirect URIs. - Regularly refresh tokens to maintain integration. - Validate anti-forgery tokens in client-side flows. --- ## Terminology - **user**: Individual with access to a Rithum account - **scope**: Area of access requested (e.g., `orders`, `inventory.readonly`) - **application ID**: Unique identifier for your application - **shared secret**: Secret generated with application ID; keep private - **redirect uri**: URI to redirect after user grants access - **response type**: `code` (Authorization Code flow) or `token` (Implicit flow) - **code**: Authorization code to exchange for tokens - **grant type**: `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, or `soap` - **refresh token**: Used to obtain new access tokens; expires after inactivity or revocation - **access token**: Used for API requests; expires in 1 hour --- For more details, see the [Developer Console](https://api.channeladvisor.com/developerconsole) or contact support. # Standard Integration Guide This guide explains how a developer would use the **ChannelAdvisor REST API** to integrate with **Rithum For Brands** for a standard integration. --- ## Prerequisites - **ChannelAdvisor Developer Account** Sign up for a Developer Key & Shared Secret here: https://complete.channeladvisor.com/DeveloperNetwork/RequestApiDevKey.aspx - **Rithum (ChannelAdvisor) Account** with Admin rights (to grant API access). - Familiarity with **REST**, **JSON**, **OAuth 2.0**, and **OData 4.0**. --- ## 1. Obtaining Developer Credentials 1. **Request a Developer Key & Shared Secret** Complete the form on the Developer Network site. You’ll receive emails to activate your account and deliver your credentials. 2. **Authorize Your Key for a Profile** In the ChannelAdvisor web portal, navigate to **My Accounts → Developer Network → Account Authorizations**, and enable access for your key. Copy your **Profile ID** (GUID) for use in API calls. --- ## 2. Authentication All REST calls require a valid **Bearer** token obtained via OAuth 2.0. ### 2.1 Obtain an Access Token ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic BASE64(:) Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=authorization_code &code= &redirect_uri= ``` *Response:* ```json { "access_token": "eyJ…", "refresh_token": "0bc…", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3599 } ``` ### 2.2 Refreshing an Access Token ```http POST https://api.channeladvisor.com/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic BASE64(:) Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=refresh_token &refresh_token= ``` ### 2.3 Using the Token Include the token in each request header: Authorization: Bearer --- ## 3. Typical Integration Flow This section outlines a common end-to-end flow for products/inventory and orders. ### 3.1 Retrieve Inventory Option A: Bulk export using Product Export (recommended for large catalogs) - Request export and download when ready. Example: request an export file (selecting fields and applying filters) ```http POST /v1/ProductExport?$filter=TotalQuantity gt 0 and startswith(SKU,'ABC') Content-Type: text/plain SKU,Name,TotalQuantity,UpdateDateUtc ``` Example: check status and download link (token from previous response) ```http GET /v1/ProductExport/CheckStatus?token={token} ``` Option B: Query products via OData ```http GET /v1/Products?$select=ID,SKU,Name,TotalQuantity,UpdateDateUtc&$filter=UpdateDateUtc ge 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z ``` Notes - Use paging via @odata.nextLink for large result sets. - Prefer Product Export for nightly or full-catalog extracts. ### 3.2 Upload/Update Inventory Option A: Create/update via Products endpoint (JSON) ```http POST /v1/Products Content-Type: application/json { "Sku": "ABC123", "Name": "Camera", "Quantity": 25, "Attributes": [ { "Name": "Color", "Value": "Black" }, { "Name": "Size", "Value": "Medium" } ] } ``` Partial updates ```http PATCH /v1/Products({productId}) Content-Type: application/json { "Quantity": 40 } ``` Option B: Bulk upload using ProductUpload (CSV or similar) - Endpoint: POST /v1/ProductUpload (multipart/form-data) - Send a file payload containing product rows (create/update). Example cURL: ``` curl -X POST "https://{host}/v1/ProductUpload" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -F "file=@products.csv;type=text/csv" ``` Tip: Use ProductUpload for high-volume updates; use Products for real-time or small deltas. ### 3.3 Retrieve Orders (Webhooks preferred) Preferred: Webhooks - Subscribe to order events to receive orders as they clear payment. See the Webhooks Guide. Polling fallback ```http GET /v1/Orders?$select=ID,ProfileID,SiteID,PaymentStatus,ShippingStatus,CreatedOnUtc&$filter=PaymentStatus eq 'Cleared' and ShippingStatus eq 'Unshipped'&exported=false ``` Paging - Use @odata.nextLink to iterate. Retrieve in batches and process incrementally. Mark orders as exported after import (to avoid re-imports) ```http POST /v1/Orders({orderId})/Export ``` Unmark if needed ```http DELETE /v1/Orders({orderId})/Export ``` ### 3.4 Process Orders (Shipments) Option A: Ship via Orders endpoint - Endpoint: POST /v1/Orders({orderId})/Ship - Supports partial shipments and item-level detail. New fulfillments are created as needed. Example ```http POST /v1/Orders(12345678)/Ship Content-Type: application/json { "TrackingNumber": "1Z999AA10123456784", "Carrier": "UPS", "Class": "Ground", "ShippedDate": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z", "Items": [ { "Sku": "ABC123", "Quantity": 1 } ] } ``` Option B: Bulk shipment upload via TrackingUpload - Endpoint: POST /v1/TrackingUpload (multipart/form-data) - Upload a file containing shipment confirmations for many orders. Example cURL ``` curl -X POST "https://{host}/v1/TrackingUpload" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -F "file=@tracking.csv;type=text/csv" ``` Typical columns include OrderID (or Seller/Marketplace order identifiers), TrackingNumber, Carrier, Class, and ShippedDate. Use this path for high-volume batch confirmations. Notes - OrdersController enforces validations (for example, delivery status cannot be set to Canceled via updates). Partial shipments and carrier/class mapping are handled by the platform. - If using bulk uploads, validate the server response and retry failures. --- ## 7. Error Handling REST API uses standard HTTP status codes and JSON error payloads: - 400 Bad Request – malformed input - 401 Unauthorized – invalid or expired token - 403 Forbidden – insufficient scope or profile disabled - 404 Not Found – resource not found - 429 Too Many Requests – rate limit exceeded Inspect the response body for fields like `errorCode`, `message`, and `details`. --- ## 8. Rate Limits - When rate limits are exceeded then the endpoint will return 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. Implement exponential backoff when retrying. --- # Shipping Labels Guide Learn how to get shipping rates, buy shipping labels, and retrieve or cancel labels using the Orders and Fulfillments APIs. --- ## Overview Shipping labels are bought through two actions on an order, and retrieved or cancelled through the fulfillment that the label belongs to: | Endpoint | Purpose | |---|---| | [`POST /v1/Orders({ID})/ShippingRates`](apidocs#tag/Orders) | Returns shipping rates for the items of an order. Can also buy the cheapest rate in the same call. | | [`POST /v1/Orders({ID})/PurchaseLabel`](apidocs#tag/Orders) | Buys a label using a `RateID` returned by `ShippingRates`. | | [`GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/Label`](apidocs#tag/Fulfillments) | Retrieves the label document of a fulfillment. | | [`DELETE /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/Label`](apidocs#tag/Fulfillments) | Cancels the shipment with the shipping partner and clears the shipping label fields of the fulfillment. | There are two ways to buy a label: - **One-step workflow** - call `ShippingRates` with `PurchaseCheapestRate: true`. The cheapest rate is bought in the same call. - **Two-step workflow** - call `ShippingRates`, choose a rate, then call `PurchaseLabel` with the chosen `RateID`. `ShippingRates` returns `200` with a `multipart/mixed` body. The rates are in one part. When a label is purchased (or an existing label is matched), the response also contains a label part and a fulfillment part. `PurchaseLabel` also returns `200` with a `multipart/mixed` body: a JSON part that describes the fulfillment (for example its ID and tracking number), followed by the label. --- ## One-Step Workflow Use the one-step workflow when you do not need to compare rates and simply want the cheapest label. ```http POST /v1/Orders(12345678)/ShippingRates Content-Type: application/json { "MeasurementUnit": "Inch", "Height": 10, "Width": 12, "Length": 12, "Weight": 1000, "WeightUnit": "Gram", "SourceFirstName": "ShipperFirstName", "SourceLastName": "ShipperLastName", "SourceAddressLine1": "100 Main Ave", "SourceCity": "Raleigh", "SourceStateOrProvince": "NC", "SourcePostalCode": "27615", "SourceCountryCode": "US", "SourcePhoneNumber": "919-555-1234", "Items": [{ "Sku": "MyTestSku", "Quantity": 1 }], "ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs": [12345], "LabelFormat": "PDF", "PurchaseCheapestRate": true, "ShippingLabelRequestID": "order-12345678-label-1" } ``` How `PurchaseCheapestRate` behaves: - A label is bought only when rates were returned and there are no errors. - Media mail and library mail rates are excluded from the purchase. - Items that are already shipped are rejected when `PurchaseCheapestRate` is `true`. - The request must resolve to a single shipping partner. If your account has more than one shipping partner that applies to the order, the API returns `400` with "PurchaseCheapestRate cannot be used when more than one shipping partner is used." Limit the request with `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs` (see [Shipping Partners](#shipping-partners)) or use the two-step workflow. > **Tip:** Replace `12345` with a `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID` from the account. You can read it from any rate in a previous `ShippingRates` response. > > Always send a `ShippingLabelRequestID` with `PurchaseCheapestRate: true`. If your request times out, repeating it with the same ID returns the label that was bought instead of buying a second one. See [ShippingLabelRequestID](#shippinglabelrequestid) below. --- ## Two-Step Workflow Use the two-step workflow when you want to review the rates before spending money. **Step 1 - get the rates.** Call `ShippingRates` without `PurchaseCheapestRate`, and with a `ShippingLabelRequestID`: ```http POST /v1/Orders(12345678)/ShippingRates Content-Type: application/json { "MeasurementUnit": "Inch", "Height": 10, "Width": 12, "Length": 12, "Weight": 1000, "WeightUnit": "Gram", "SourceFirstName": "ShipperFirstName", "SourceLastName": "ShipperLastName", "SourceAddressLine1": "100 Main Ave", "SourceCity": "Raleigh", "SourceStateOrProvince": "NC", "SourcePostalCode": "27615", "SourceCountryCode": "US", "SourcePhoneNumber": "919-555-1234", "Items": [{ "Sku": "MyTestSku", "Quantity": 1 }], "DeliveryConfirmation": "NoDeliveryConfirmation", "LabelFormat": "PDF", "ShippingLabelRequestID": "order-12345678-label-1" } ``` Each rate in the response has a `RateID`. A rate is valid for 1800 seconds; the remaining time is returned in `ExpiresInSeconds`. **Step 2 - buy the label.** Call `PurchaseLabel` with the `RateID` you chose, the same `ShippingLabelRequestID`, and a `LabelFormat`: ```http POST /v1/Orders(12345678)/PurchaseLabel Content-Type: application/json { "RateID": "3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301", "LabelFormat": "PDF", "ShippingLabelRequestID": "order-12345678-label-1" } ``` Things to know about `PurchaseLabel`: - It accepts only `RateID`, `LabelFormat`, and `ShippingLabelRequestID`. - `LabelFormat` is **required** and must be `PDF` or `ZPL`. If you omit it, the API returns `400` with the message "LabelFormat is required." Unlike `ShippingRates`, there is no default. - An expired or unknown `RateID` returns `400`. Request new rates and try again. - Once a rate has been purchased, it is deleted from the cache and cannot be bought again. > **Tip:** `LabelFormat` on `ShippingRates` defaults to `PDF`, but on `PurchaseLabel` it must always be sent. **What a purchase does to the order.** Buying a label marks the items shipped. The API creates a shipped fulfillment with the carrier, class, `ShippedDateUTC`, tracking number, and a delivery status of `Complete` (a partial shipment), and then saves the label. This applies to `PurchaseLabel` and to `PurchaseCheapestRate: true`. > **Tip:** Buy a label only when you are ready to ship. The purchase itself records the shipment, so you do not need a separate call to mark the items shipped. --- ## Shipping Partners Partners that do not apply to the order are always excluded: Amazon shipping is not used for orders that did not come from Amazon, and Walmart shipping is not used for orders that did not come from Walmart. By default, `ShippingRates` requests rates from every remaining active shipping label partner account. Each rate in the response includes a `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID`. To limit a request to specific partner accounts, send their IDs in `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs`: ```json { "ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs": [12345] } ``` An ID that does not belong to the account returns `400` with "ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID N does not exist." `PurchaseCheapestRate` can only be used when the request resolves to one shipping partner. Several accounts of the same partner are fine. With more than one partner, the API returns `400` with "PurchaseCheapestRate cannot be used when more than one shipping partner is used." Either limit the request with `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountIDs`, or use the [two-step workflow](#two-step-workflow) and choose a rate yourself. > **Tip:** Not sure which ID to use? Request rates without `PurchaseCheapestRate` first, and read the `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID` of the rate you want. --- ## ShippingLabelRequestID `ShippingLabelRequestID` is a value you choose to identify a label request. It is what makes label requests safe to retry. - It can be at most 50 characters long. - It is stored on the fulfillment, but it is not returned in the response. - **On `PurchaseLabel`:** reusing an ID returns the existing label instead of buying another one. - **On `ShippingRates`:** reusing an ID that was already used to buy a label returns the rates that were cached for that ID (rates are kept for 30 days). A label is returned only when `PurchaseCheapestRate` is `true`. If the cached rates are missing, the rates part of the response is empty. - **A new ID skips the match.** Using an ID the API has not seen before skips the lookup and treats the call as a brand new request. - "No open items" errors can occur only when `PurchaseCheapestRate` is `true`. > **Tip:** Generate the ID from something stable in your own system, such as the order ID plus a package number, so a retry after a timeout reuses the same value. --- ## DeliveryConfirmation `DeliveryConfirmation` is a `ShippingRates` parameter. It defaults to `NoDeliveryConfirmation` when omitted. `PurchaseLabel` does not accept it. | Value | Meaning | |---|---| | `NoDeliveryConfirmation` | No delivery confirmation. This is the default. | | `SignatureRequired` | A signature is required on delivery. | | `AdultSignatureRequired` | An adult signature is required on delivery. | | `Default` | Accepted value, but it is not the default of the `ShippingRates` parameter. | `DeliveryConfirmation` is passed to the shipping partner. How it is applied depends on the shipping partner. > **Tip:** Do not copy `Default` into your requests expecting "the default behavior". Omit the field, or send `NoDeliveryConfirmation`, to get the default. --- ## DeliverByDate Set `ApplyDeliverByDate` to `true` on `ShippingRates` to return only rates that deliver on or before a deadline, and provide the deadline in `DeliverByDateUtc`: ```json { "ApplyDeliverByDate": true, "DeliverByDateUtc": "2026-11-05T00:00:00Z" } ``` If you omit `DeliverByDateUtc`, the delivery-by date of the order is used. If neither is available, the API returns `400`. --- ## Item Selection The `Items` array tells `ShippingRates` what is going into the package. - `Items` is required, and the `Quantity` of every entry must be greater than 0. - Each entry identifies the item by `FulfillmentItemID`, `OrderItemID`, or `Sku`. At least one of the three must be provided. - Unshipped items are prioritized when the API matches your entries to the order. - With `PurchaseCheapestRate: true`, items that are already shipped are rejected. - Items and quantities are checked when rates are requested, not when `PurchaseLabel` is called. If an item or quantity is rejected, fix it in the `ShippingRates` call. **Optional parameters.** `Weight`, `WeightUnit`, `MeasurementUnit`, the package dimensions, `DistributionCenterID`, and `PackageID` are all optional in the request schema. Dimensions are taken from `PackageID` if it is present; otherwise provide height, length, and width together. An unknown `DistributionCenterID` returns `400` with "DistributionCenterID N does not exist.", and an unknown `PackageID` returns `400` with "PackageID N does not exist." Other `ShippingRates` validation errors return `400`: `LabelFormat` must be `PDF` or `ZPL`, `Items` must not be empty ("At least one item needs to be included."), and `ShippingLabelRequestID` can be at most 50 characters. --- ## Retrieving and Cancelling a Label Labels belong to fulfillments. The JSON part of a `PurchaseLabel` response includes the fulfillment ID (`FulfillmentID`). **Retrieve a label** ```http GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/Label ``` | Endpoint | 404 | 410 | |---|---|---| | `GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/Label` | The fulfillment does not exist or has no label. | The personally identifiable information was removed. | | `GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/ReturnLabel` | The fulfillment has no return label. | The personally identifiable information was removed. | | `GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/ChannelReturnLabel` | The fulfillment has no channel return label. | Not returned. | | `GET /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/ChannelPackingSlip` | The fulfillment has no channel packing slip. | Not returned. | **Cancel a label** ```http DELETE /v1/Fulfillments({ID})/Label?unshipfulfillment=true ``` - Cancels the shipment with the shipping partner, then clears the shipping label fields on the fulfillment. - Returns `204` on success, and `404` when the fulfillment does not exist or has no label. - Returns `400` with the failure message when the cancellation fails, for example "The shipment did not have a valid shipping label", "The shipment did not have a valid shipping partner setup configured.", or an error message from the shipping partner. - `unshipfulfillment` is optional. When it is `true`, the fulfillment delivery status is set to `NoChange` (unshipped) as part of the cancellation. --- ## Error Handling | Status | Typical cause | |---|---| | `400` | `LabelFormat` missing on `PurchaseLabel`; expired or unknown `RateID`; `ApplyDeliverByDate` set to `true` when neither `DeliverByDateUtc` nor a delivery-by date on the order is available; invalid items or quantities on `ShippingRates`; no usable shipping partner for the account or order; an unknown `ShippingLabelPartnerAccountID`; `PurchaseCheapestRate` with more than one shipping partner; a failed label cancellation on `DELETE`. | | `404` | Fulfillment or label, return label, channel return label, or channel packing slip not found on the fulfillment. | | `410` | The label or return label is no longer available because the personally identifiable information was removed. | Other behavior to plan for: - Rates expire after 1800 seconds. If `PurchaseLabel` returns `400` for a `RateID` you recently received, request new rates. - Reusing a `ShippingLabelRequestID` is the safe way to retry. See [ShippingLabelRequestID](#shippinglabelrequestid). - "No open items" errors occur only when `PurchaseCheapestRate` is `true`. Inspect the response body for details about what failed. --- ## Additional Resources - [Orders Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Orders-Guide) - [Release Notes](apidocs#tag/Releases) # API Rate limiting Guide ## General REST API Limits REST API requests of all types and to all endpoints are limited in the following ways: 1. **IP Address** - **500,000** requests per hour - **8,300** requests per minute 2. **Account** (this is also known as Profile within Rithum) - **2,000** requests per minute. This limit is per profile, regardless of the developer key, application, or integration making the API request. 3. **Integration** - **5** concurrent requests --- ## Endpoint-Specific Limits #### `/v1/ProductUpload` Endpoint - Maximum data payload size: **128** MB - Maximum rate limit: **60** files per hour per account (profile) #### `/v1/ProductExport` Endpoint - Maximum: **10,000,000** products exported per day - Maximum: **10** requests per minute - Additional export requests will be rejected with HTTP status `429 Too Many Requests`. > **Note:** Ignoring the violation of request limits may lead to the offender being blocked from submitting further requests. #### `/v1/Webhooks/RetryFailedEvents` - Maximum rate limit: **5** requests per hour per Webhook ID --- ## Illustrating the General REST API Limits Multiple client integrations and multiple profiles illustrate different integration approaches to accommodate the three different limits. ![Rate Limiting Flow](data:image/png;base64,) --- ## Building Efficient Integrations The Developer Network has a lot of content to aid in building efficient integrations. Some of these will help avoid violating the request limits, and some are just good practice: - **[Product Uploads](/apidocs#tag/ProductUpload):** Outlines delivery of product files through the API. - Recommended for updating products in large catalogs. - Most helpful method to avoid hitting the request limits, as it utilizes file format upload (delivered via API) to update product data instead of individual requests. - **[Product Exports](/apidocs#tag/ProductExport):** Defines a method to export data via API. - **[Product ID Integrations](/apidocs#tag/Products/operation/Products.Product.GetProduct):** Focuses on ensuring efficient handling of Product IDs. - May help avoid request limits depending on need, catalog size, and system design. - **[Batch Requests](/apidocs/#tag/Guides/Batch-Requests-Guide):** Defines how requests can be batched together (doesn't help with avoiding request limits).

This page contains release notes for changes to the Rithum For Brands REST API and Webhooks. Each entry includes the release date and a summary of the change. Use this log to track new features, improvements, and deprecations.

---

## Release History

### 2026

#### June
- Added: New `OrderModified` webhook event for order, item, and fulfillment changes. (*June 18th 2026*)
  - See [Webhooks Guide](#tag/Guides/Webhooks-Guide).

#### May
- Added: New `AssemblyBundleDistributionCenters` field to `POST /v1/Products`. Required when `BundleType` is `AssemblyBundleItem`. Fixes an issue where assembly bundles were silently created as standard bundles. (*May 20th 2026*)
  - See [Products & Inventory Guide](#tag/Guides/Products-and-Inventory-Guide).
- Added: New `ExternallyManagedFulfillmentCompleted` webhook event for externally-managed distribution centers. (*May 20th 2026*)
  - See [Webhooks Guide](#tag/Guides/Webhooks-Guide).

#### February
- Added: new `v1/Orders(id)/SubstituteItems` endpoint. Allows the ability to substitute existing items with new items. (*Feb 2nd 2026*)
  - Currently only enabled for Checkout Direct and DoorDash marketplaces

### 2025

#### October
- Added: New `v1/users` and `v1/usergroups` endpoints for managing users through the REST API. (*Oct 1st 2025*)
  - Requires new scope `users`.  
  - This feature is currently invite only. 
- Added: New `IsRma` property to `OrderAdjustment` and `OrderItemAdjustment` models as well as webhooks and streams.  (*Oct 2nd 2025*)
  - Filterable on `GET` requests

#### September
- Added: New `v1/Orders(id)/ProcessAdjustment` endpoint to allow for actioning adjustments using the `SiteAdjustmentID` identifier. (*Sept 22nd 2025*)
  - Will operate on all adjustments for an order that match the supplied `SiteAdjustmentID`

#### July
- Added: New Order entity properties for `ShippingAddressType` and `ShippingBusinessHours` to improve shipping accuracy for Amazon Business orders. Supported in REST API and Webhooks. (*July 14th 2025*)
- Added: New `v1/Listings` and `v1/listingerrorrollups` endpoints for retrieving marketplace listing and error information. (*July 2nd 2025*)

#### May
- Added: New authentication options for webhooks. See Create and Manage Authentication and Security & verification. (*May 21st 2025*)

#### April
- Added: New `Streams` endpoints for efficient RMA integrations. See Streams overview. (*April 23rd 2025*)

#### March
- Added: `TrackingUpload` endpoints for bulk shipment requests and shipping templates. (*March 26th 2025*)

#### February
- Added: `LastUpdatedDateUtc` property added to `OrderAdjustments` and `OrderItemAdjustments`. (*February 27th 2025*)
- Added: New `Tags` entity added to Orders for filterable `OrderTags`. (*February 19th 2025*)

#### January
- Added: New `ReturnShippingCost`, `ReturnTrackingNumberOrUrl`, and `ReturnShippingMethod` properties for adjustments. (*January 28th 2025*)
