### Types of products
A product in the platform can be one of the following types:
	 
| Type       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Buyable | Has Quantity      |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------|-------------------|
| Standalone | The default type of product.Can be listed and purchased without impact to other products.May be a component in a Bundle. When component in a Bundle, quantity changes will impact available quantity in the Bundle.                                                                                                                                                                                    |  Yes    | Yes               |
| Parent     | A container for one or more child items that vary by one or more attributes such as size or color.A parent does not have quantity and is not purchasable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | No      | No                |
| Child      | A child product can be purchased and is always related to a single parent product.A child product usually exists for each variation of a parent product.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Yes     | Yes               |
| Bundle     | Bundles are a virtual container for one or more other buyable items. For example, a bundle may contain one camera and two memory cards. Each bundle component, which can be either a standalone or child product, has a component multiplier quantity, which is used to calculate the bundle's overall quantity.                                                                                       | Yes     | Yes (calculated)  |
	 
### Flow of product creation
	 
Outline the process of creating products (as a general concept)
* Client provides new SKU data to the system at will.
* Some pre-requisites may need to be in place depending on design of the client products:
* Variation names/types
* Distribution Centers
* During creation of SKUs, apply all known product attributes within the same product creation request for ease of use.  Otherwise individual attribute requests are required to append new attributes.
* Apply quantity information to products.
* Once a product has been created, these are the options going forward:
	 
| Operation               | Description                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CREATE Bundles          | The products need to be applied to bundles for sale.                                                                            |
| UPDATE Field Data       | Data needs to be adjusted for an existing product in an existing field.                                                         |
| ADD More Data           | Data needs to be added to an existing product in an existing field, or a new field, and data needs to be added for a product.   |
| DELETE Individual Data  | A data point needs to be cleared of the existing values, leaving a blank.                                                       |
| DELETE the Entire Product | Remove a product from the system because it is no longer active.                                                              |
| UPLOAD Product Data     | Same as ADD and UPDATE, but executed in bulk.                                                                                   |
| EXPORT Product Data     | Extract data in bulk.                                                                                                           |

tags.name: AttributeValues
tags.description:
Attribute Values store name/value pairs for a product. Use these endpoints to add, update, or remove attributes for a product.

Key capabilities:
- Create a new attribute value for a product.
- Get, update, or delete an existing attribute value.
- Use OData $select, $filter, $orderby, $count where supported.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/AttributeValues` - Create a new attribute value.
- `GET v1/AttributeValues(Name='{name}',ProductID={productID})` - Get a specific attribute value.
- `PATCH v1/AttributeValues(Name='{name}',ProductID={productID})` - Update an attribute value.
- `DELETE v1/AttributeValues(Name='{name}',ProductID={productID})` - Remove an attribute value.

Notes:
- Keys are composite: Name and ProductID.
- When updating, only include fields you want to change.

tags.name: ProductLabels
tags.description:
Labels let you tag products with custom strings for grouping, filtering, and workflow. Use this to add, update, or remove labels for a product.

Key capabilities:
- Manage labels for a product by name.
- Add or update a label value.
- Remove an existing label from a product.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Products({productID})/Labels('{name}')` - Get a product label.
- `PUT v1/Products({productID})/Labels('{name}')` - Create or update a product label.
- `DELETE v1/Products({productID})/Labels('{name}')` - Remove a product label.

Notes:
- Provide productID and label name in the route.
- For integrations with multiple profiles, include ProfileID where required by your workflow.

tags.name: ProductBundleComponents
tags.description:
Bundle Components represent child SKUs that make up a bundle product. Use these endpoints to view or modify the relationship between a bundle and its components.

Key capabilities:
- Retrieve a specific bundle component for a product.
- Create/update or delete a bundle component assignment.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Products({productID})/BundleComponents({componentID})` - Get a bundle component mapping.
- `PUT v1/Products({productID})/BundleComponents({componentID})` - Create or update a mapping.
- `DELETE v1/Products({productID})/BundleComponents({componentID})` - Remove a mapping.

Notes:
- productID is the parent (bundle) product; componentID is the child item.
- Be mindful of inventory implications when changing bundle composition.

tags.name: ProductUpload
tags.description:
Product Upload lets you send a file to create or update product data in bulk. The upload is processed asynchronously and returns a token you can use to poll status.

Key capabilities:
- Upload a product file using multipart/form-data.
- Check processing status using the returned token.
- Handle throttling and retry on 429 responses.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/ProductUpload` - Upload file (multipart/form-data, field name: uploadFile).
- `GET v1/ProductUpload?token={token}` - Check upload status.

Notes:
- Large files are queued and processed; do not poll too frequently.
- If your integration has access to multiple profiles, include profileId in the request.

tags.name: ProductExport
tags.description:
Export product data in bulk using server-side filters. Exports are queued and processed asynchronously and return a token to poll status.

Key capabilities:
- Request an export for a subset of products with OData-like filters.
- Control which fields are included by providing a comma-separated field list in the request body.
- Poll for export status using the returned token.
- Retrieve status and final location once ready or archived.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/ProductExport` - Start a new export (supports $filter and optional ProfileID).
- `GET v1/ProductExport?token={token}` - Check export status.

Notes:
- Exports are throttled and processed in order; avoid rapid polling.
- Daily limits and per-minute request limits apply; handle HTTP 429 with backoff.
- Large exports can be archived; check for HTTP 410 when polling.

## POST Request Body Format

The `POST /v1/ProductExport` endpoint accepts an **optional** `text/plain` body containing a comma-separated list of field names to include in the exported file.

**Content-Type:** `text/plain`

**Body format:** A comma-separated list of field names (no spaces required around commas).

**Example body:**
```
id,sku,title,totalquantity,attr:size,attr:color
```

**If the body is omitted or empty:** All available product fields are exported.

**Output format:** The exported file is tab-delimited.

### Field Name Examples

| Field name | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Product ID |
| `sku` | Product SKU |
| `title` | Product title |
| `totalquantity` | Total available quantity |
| `attr:size` | Custom attribute named "size" |
| `attr:color` | Custom attribute named "color" |

Prefix custom attributes with `attr:` followed by the attribute name.

### Important: Do Not Send JSON

The body must be `text/plain`. Sending `Content-Type: application/json` with a JSON body will cause unexpected failures. This is a common source of integration errors — see the [Release Notes](apidocs#tag/Releases) for historical context.

tags.name: Images
tags.description:
Images represent product images by placement. Manage image URLs per product and placement name.

Key capabilities:
- List, create, update, and delete image records.
- Navigate to related product entity.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Images` - List images.
- `GET v1/Images(PlacementName='{placement}',ProductID={productID})` - Get a specific image.
- `POST v1/Images` - Create an image record.
- `PATCH v1/Images(PlacementName='{placement}',ProductID={productID})` - Update an image.
- `DELETE v1/Images(PlacementName='{placement}',ProductID={productID})` - Delete an image.

Notes:
- Keys are composite: PlacementName and ProductID.
- PlacementName identifies the image slot (e.g., Main, Alternate1).

tags.name: DCQuantities
tags.description:
DC Quantities provide per-distribution-center inventory quantities for products.

Key capabilities:
- Create DC quantity entries.
- Get, update, or delete a specific DC quantity (composite key).

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/DCQuantities` - Create a DC quantity.
- `GET v1/DCQuantities(DistributionCenterID={dcId},ProductID={productId})` - Get a specific quantity record.
- `PATCH v1/DCQuantities(DistributionCenterID={dcId},ProductID={productId})` - Update a quantity record.
- `DELETE v1/DCQuantities(DistributionCenterID={dcId},ProductID={productId})` - Remove a quantity record.

Notes:
- Keys are composite: DistributionCenterID and ProductID.
- Use $select and $filter to narrow results when listing.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description:
Orders capture purchases from marketplaces and custom sources. Use the Orders endpoints to retrieve, update, ship, and document orders.

Key capabilities:
- Query orders with rich OData filters and expansions.
- Ship orders, purchase labels, and compute shipping rates.
- Confirm or deny orders for marketplace acknowledgement flows.
- Access related items, fulfillments, adjustments, custom fields, and documents.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Orders` - List orders with OData query options.
- `GET v1/Orders({id})` - Get an order.
- `PATCH v1/Orders({id})` - Update an order.
- `POST v1/Orders/Create` - Create a new order.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/Ship` - Mark as shipped or purchase labels.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/ShippingRates` - Get shipping rates, and optionally buy the cheapest one.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/PurchaseLabel` - Purchase a label using a `RateID` from ShippingRates.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/Export` - Export order to CSV-like format.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/Confirm` - Confirm receipt of an order.
- `POST v1/Orders({id})/Deny` - Deny (reject) an order.

Notes:
- Many properties are marketplace-specific; plan for nulls.
- Paging uses @odata.nextLink; avoid hardcoded $skip.
- For label workflows, see the [Shipping Labels Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Shipping-Labels-Guide).

## Shipping Status Values

The `ShippingStatus` field on the Order entity reflects the order's current shipping state. Valid values:

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Unshipped` | Fulfillment is incomplete. This is the default value. |
| `Shipped` | Fulfillment is complete. |
| `PartiallyShipped` | Fulfillment is incomplete. |
| `PendingShipment` | Fulfillment is incomplete. |
| `Canceled` | Fulfillment is complete. |
| `ThirdPartyManaged` | Fulfillment is complete. |

tags.name: OrderItems
tags.description:
Order Items are line items within an order. Use these endpoints to retrieve items, navigate relationships, and adjust item-level amounts.

Key capabilities:
- Query order items and expand related entities.
- Adjust a specific item (refunds, restocks, etc.).

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/OrderItems` - List order items.
- `GET v1/OrderItems({id})` - Get a specific order item.
- `POST v1/OrderItems({id})/Adjust` - Create an adjustment for the item.

Notes:
- Use $expand=BundleComponents,FulfillmentItems,Promotions,Adjustments to navigate related data.
- Item titles and SKUs may differ from inventory depending on marketplace.

tags.name: OrderAdjustments
tags.description:
Order Adjustments capture order-level refunds, returns, and fee changes. Use actions to approve or reject buyer requests and returns.

Key capabilities:
- Retrieve and update adjustments.
- Approve or reject buyer requests and returns.
- Generate return shipping labels when supported.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/OrderAdjustments({id})` - Get an adjustment.
- `PATCH v1/OrderAdjustments({id})` - Update an adjustment.
- `POST v1/OrderAdjustments({id})/ApproveBuyerRequest` - Approve a buyer request.
- `POST v1/OrderAdjustments({id})/RejectBuyerRequest` - Reject a buyer request.
- `POST v1/OrderAdjustments({id})/ApproveReturn` - Approve a return.
- `POST v1/OrderAdjustments({id})/RejectReturn` - Reject a return.
- `POST v1/OrderAdjustments({id})/ReturnShippingLabel` - Create a return shipping label.

Notes:
- Some fields are marketplace-dependent and may be null.
- Use appropriate Reason codes per marketplace (see Sites).

tags.name: OrderItemAdjustments
tags.description:
Order Item Adjustments represent refunds, returns, and quantity changes at the line-item level.

Key capabilities:
- Retrieve or update an item-level adjustment.
- Approve or reject buyer requests and returns.
- Generate a return shipping label when supported.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})` - Get an item adjustment.
- `PATCH v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})` - Update an item adjustment.
- `POST v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})/ApproveBuyerRequest` - Approve a buyer request.
- `POST v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})/RejectBuyerRequest` - Reject a buyer request.
- `POST v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})/ApproveReturn` - Approve a return (requires ConditionQuantityList).
- `POST v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})/RejectReturn` - Reject a return (supports ConditionQuantityList).
- `POST v1/OrderItemAdjustments({id})/ReturnShippingLabel` - Create a return shipping label.

Notes:
- Use valid Reason codes per marketplace (see Sites endpoint).
- Many fields are marketplace-dependent and may be null.
- Use $select/$expand to limit payloads and include relationships.

tags.name: Fulfillments
tags.description:
Fulfillments represent shipments or pickup/delivery actions for an order.

Key capabilities:
- Retrieve, create, update, and delete fulfillments.
- Confirm or deny fulfillment actions; move items between fulfillments.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Fulfillments` - List fulfillments.
- `GET v1/Fulfillments({id})` - Get a specific fulfillment.
- `POST v1/Fulfillments` - Create a fulfillment.
- `PATCH v1/Fulfillments({id})` - Update a fulfillment.
- `DELETE v1/Fulfillments({id})` - Delete a fulfillment.
- `POST v1/Fulfillments({id})/Confirm` - Confirm a fulfillment.
- `POST v1/Fulfillments({id})/Deny` - Deny a fulfillment.
- `POST v1/Fulfillments({id})/Move` - Move items to another fulfillment.
- `GET v1/Fulfillments({id})/Label` - Get the shipping label.
- `DELETE v1/Fulfillments({id})/Label` - Cancel the shipping label.
- `GET v1/Fulfillments({id})/ReturnLabel` - Get the return shipping label.
- `GET v1/Fulfillments({id})/ChannelReturnLabel` - Get the channel return shipping label.
- `GET v1/Fulfillments({id})/ChannelPackingSlip` - Get the channel packing slip.

Notes:
- Use $expand=Order,Items to include related data.
- Some fields are system-calculated and read-only.
- For label workflows, see the [Shipping Labels Guide](apidocs#tag/Guides/Shipping-Labels-Guide).

## Delivery Status Values

The `DeliveryStatus` field on the Fulfillment entity tracks the current delivery state. Valid values:

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `NoChange` | The fulfillment is unshipped. Making a request with this value will set a fulfillment or order to unshipped. |
| `InTransit` | The fulfillment is in transit to a location where the recipient may pick it up. Used for eBay In-Store-Pickup orders. |
| `ReadyForPickup` | The fulfillment has arrived at the pickup location and is ready for the recipient to pick up. Used for eBay In-Store-Pickup orders. |
| `Complete` | The fulfillment is complete and/or fully shipped. |
| `Canceled` | The items on this fulfillment have been canceled and will not be fulfilled. |
| `ThirdPartyManaged` | The fulfillment is handled outside Rithum. Integrations where orders are imported into Rithum but the retailer does not want Rithum to manage any aspects of the order's fulfillment will have this status. |
| `Confirmed` | The fulfillment location confirms receipt of the order. |
| `PickAndPack` | The items in the fulfillment are in the process of being retrieved and packed. |
| `LabelCreated` | The items in the fulfillment are packed and a label has been generated for pickup or retrieval. |
| `Held` | The fulfillment is in Held status when decisions are needed for change in the fulfillment. Refer to Hold All Seller Fulfillments setting. |
| `Delivered` | The shipment was delivered to the final destination. |
| `FailedDelivery` | The shipment failed delivery to the final destination. |

tags.name: FulfillmentItems
tags.description:
Fulfillment Items represent individual items within a fulfillment. Manage item-level shipping, costs, and references.

Key capabilities:
- List and retrieve fulfillment items.
- Move an item to another fulfillment.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/FulfillmentItems` - List fulfillment items.
- `GET v1/FulfillmentItems({id})` - Get a specific fulfillment item.
- `POST v1/FulfillmentItems({id})/Move` - Move this item to another fulfillment.

Notes:
- Use $expand=Fulfillment,OrderItem to include related details.
- Several cost fields may be non-sortable or restricted.

tags.name: TrackingUpload
tags.description:
Tracking Upload lets you submit a file of shipment tracking numbers to update orders in bulk. Processing is asynchronous and returns a token.

Key capabilities:
- Upload tracking file via multipart/form-data.
- Check status of an upload using a token.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/TrackingUpload` - Upload a tracking file (field: uploadFile).
- `GET v1/TrackingUpload?token={token}` - Check status of an upload.

Notes:
- Respect throttling; backoff on 429.
- Include profileid if the integration has access to multiple profiles.

tags.name: ChannelDocuments
tags.description:
Channel Documents are marketplace-required documents such as VAT invoices. Upload or retrieve documents and mark them as retrieved once consumed.

Key capabilities:
- Upload a document (binary content) or create a specialized document type.
- List or retrieve documents by key.
- Mark a document as retrieved.
- List documents that are not yet supplied.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/ChannelDocuments` - List channel documents.
- `POST v1/ChannelDocuments` - Upload a document (application/pdf or specialized model).
- `GET v1/ChannelDocuments({DocumentKey})` - Get a document.
- `PATCH v1/ChannelDocuments({DocumentKey})` - Update document fields.
- `POST v1/ChannelDocuments({DocumentKey})/Retrieved` - Mark as retrieved.
- `GET v1/ChannelDocuments/NotSupplied()` - List orders requiring documents.

Notes:
- Use appropriate MimeType and DocumentType when creating.
- For Amazon VAT, use the specialized AmazonVATInvoice model.

tags.name: OrderDocuments
tags.description:
Order Documents are artifacts associated with an order, such as invoices, packing slips, and return labels.

Key capabilities:
- List or retrieve order documents.
- Mark a document as retrieved to update downstream workflows.
- Get lightweight metadata with Orders(OrderID)/OrderDocuments().

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/OrderDocuments` - List order documents.
- `GET v1/OrderDocuments(DocumentKey='{key}',OrderID={orderId})` - Get a specific document.
- `PATCH v1/OrderDocuments(DocumentKey='{key}',OrderID={orderId})` - Update document fields.
- `DELETE v1/OrderDocuments(DocumentKey='{key}',OrderID={orderId})` - Delete a document.
- `POST v1/OrderDocuments(DocumentKey='{key}',OrderID={orderId})/Retrieved` - Mark as retrieved.
- `GET v1/Orders({orderId})/OrderDocuments()` - Get light-weight flyweight docs for an order.

Notes:
- Some document types are marketplace-provided and read-only.
- Use $select to avoid returning large Content fields unless needed.

tags.name: Packages
tags.description:
Packages define reusable packing configurations (dimensions, weight, and other shipment parameters) for shipping calculations and labels.

Key capabilities:
- Store standard package dimensions and weights.
- Reference packages when requesting shipping rates or labels.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Packages` - List packages.
- `GET v1/Packages({id})` - Get a specific package.
- `POST v1/Packages` - Create a package.
- `PATCH v1/Packages({id})` - Update a package.
- `DELETE v1/Packages({id})` - Delete a package.

Notes:
- Use consistent units (MeasurementUnit/WeightUnit) when providing dimensions and weight.

tags.name: CustomFields
tags.description:
Custom Fields let you store additional data on orders using predefined field IDs. Values can be created, updated, or removed.

Key capabilities:
- Create or update a custom field value for an order.
- Retrieve or delete a specific custom field value.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/CustomFields` - Create or update a custom field value.
- `GET v1/CustomFields(FieldID={fieldId},OrderID={orderId})` - Get a specific custom field.
- `PATCH v1/CustomFields(FieldID={fieldId},OrderID={orderId})` - Update a custom field.
- `DELETE v1/CustomFields(FieldID={fieldId},OrderID={orderId})` - Remove a custom field.

Notes:
- FieldID is defined in the profile; OrderID identifies the order.
- Provide ProfileID if your access token spans multiple profiles.

tags.name: Adjustments
tags.description:
The Adjustments tag covers non-OData adjustment utilities like acknowledge/unacknowledge operations for async workflows.

Key capabilities:
- Acknowledge an adjustment.
- Unacknowledge an adjustment (it will appear again in unacknowledged queries).

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/adjustments({id})/acknowledge` - Acknowledge an adjustment.
- `DELETE v1/adjustments({id})/acknowledge` - Unacknowledge an adjustment.

Notes:
- Use ShouldEvictOnAdjustmentChange to re-surface adjustments on status changes (helpful for RMAs).

tags.name: Profiles
tags.description:
Profiles represent selling accounts or storefronts within your integration. Many requests require a ProfileID when multiple profiles are accessible.

Key capabilities:
- List or retrieve profiles.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Profiles` - List profiles.
- `GET v1/Profiles({id})` - Get a specific profile.

tags.name: DistributionCenters
tags.description:
Distribution Centers represent the physical or virtual locations that fulfill orders. Use these endpoints to manage distribution center metadata and hours.

Key capabilities:
- List, create, update, and delete distribution centers.
- Query and expand related OperatingHours.
- Filter and sort with OData query options.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/DistributionCenters` - List distribution centers.
- `GET v1/DistributionCenters({id})` - Get a specific distribution center.
- `POST v1/DistributionCenters` - Create a distribution center.
- `PATCH v1/DistributionCenters({id})` - Update a distribution center.
- `DELETE v1/DistributionCenters({id})` - Delete a distribution center.

Notes:
- Include related OperatingHours with $expand=OperatingHours when needed.
- Some properties are marketplace-specific or nullable.

tags.name: DistributionCentersUpload
tags.description:
Upload a file to create or update Distribution Centers in bulk. The upload is processed asynchronously and returns a token for status checks.

Key capabilities:
- Upload a distribution centers file via multipart/form-data.
- Check processing status using a token.
- Supports template-driven uploads.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/DCUpload` - Upload distribution centers file (field: uploadFile).
- `GET v1/DCUpload?token={token}` - Check upload status.

Notes:
- Use the correct delimiter/extension to match the file format.
- Handle HTTP 429 with exponential backoff.

tags.name: OperatingHours
tags.description:
Operating Hours define daily open/close times for a distribution center. Use these to support pickup, delivery, and SLA calculations.

Key capabilities:
- List and create operating hours records.
- Filter, sort, and select fields with OData options.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/OperatingHours` - List operating hours.
- `POST v1/OperatingHours` - Create operating hours.

Notes:
- Each record is associated with a DistributionCenterID and day.
- Use $filter=DistributionCenterID eq {id} to retrieve hours for a specific DC.

Working hours are defined using the 24-hour format. For example, 8am to 5pm is represented as `08:00` to `17:00`.

Each operating hours record returns:
- `DistributionCenterID`: The DC this record applies to.
- `Day`: The day of the week (1 = Sunday, 2 = Monday, � 7 = Saturday).
- `OpenTime`: The time the center opens.
- `CloseTime`: The time the center closes.
- `TimeZone`: The timezone of the operating hours.

Example response for a specific DC (`DistributionCenterID` = 123) on Monday:
```json
{
  "DistributionCenterID": 123,
  "Day": 2,
  "OpenTime": "08:00",
  "CloseTime": "17:00",
  "TimeZone": "GMT-5"
}
```

tags.name: Batch
tags.description:
Submit multiple API requests in a single HTTP call using the OData multipart/mixed batch format. Each request in the batch is processed independently and the response contains the individual results.

Key details:
- Maximum of 100 individual requests per batch.
- Uses `multipart/mixed` content type with boundary delimiters.
- Each request must include the full URL, HTTP method, and any required headers.
- Refer to the Batch Requests guide for full formatting details and examples.

Endpoints overview:
- `POST v1/$batch` - Submit a batch of individual API requests.

tags.name: Listings
tags.description:
Listings provide product-level listing diagnostics by product ID, including marketplace errors.

Key capabilities:
- Retrieve listing errors for a product across marketplaces.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/listings/productid/{productId}/errors` - Get listing errors for a product.

Notes:
- Provide profileid if your access token has access to multiple profiles.
- Use page and pagesize for pagination.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description:
Sites enumerate supported marketplaces and their capabilities (e.g., adjustment reasons). Use this to tailor behavior per channel.

Key capabilities:
- List sites and inspect properties like AdjustmentReasons.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Sites` - List sites.
- `GET v1/Sites({id})` - Get a specific site.

Notes:
- Use the Site's AdjustmentReasons to determine valid values for cancellations/refunds.

tags.name: Streams
tags.description:
Streams provide a way to receive event notifications for your integration in near real-time. A stream aggregates events (such as buyer initiated return updates) and assigns a monotonically increasing position to each event so you can resume processing reliably.

Key capabilities:
- List streams for your integration and inspect their status.
- Create a new stream and select which event types you want to subscribe to.
- Enable or disable an existing stream.
- Delete a stream when it is no longer needed.
- Read events from a specific position with pagination semantics.
- Retrieve a specific event by its position.

Endpoints overview:
- `GET v1/Streams` - Retrieve all streams for the integration.
- `GET v1/Streams({streamID})` - Retrieve a single stream by ID.
- `POST v1/Streams` - Create a new stream.
- `PATCH v1/Streams({streamID})` - Update the stream status.
- `DELETE v1/Streams({streamID})` - Delete a stream.
- `GET v1/Streams({streamID})/{startingPostion}` - Read events starting at the given position.
- `GET v1/Streams({streamID})/Event/{positionID}` - Retrieve a specific event.

Notes:
- Positions are inclusive; requesting position N returns the event at N if present.
- Event reads are limited in batch size to promote responsiveness.
- Ensure your integration maintains and persists the last processed position for reliable consumption.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
### User & Group Management Overview
The User Management API enables managing platform users, their group memberships, and viewing the security modules granted through a specific group.
 
 ### Important Note
 The user that authorizes the REST API integration will be the user that is creating and managing other users via these endpoints.  So created users will have at most the same permissions as that user.

### Core Concepts
| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| User | Represents an individual that can log in and act within a Profile (tenant/account). A user must belong to at least one group. |
| Group | A collection that grants access (modules/permissions). Users inherit capabilities through their groups. |
| Module | A security module (permission area) associated with a group. A user’s effective permissions are the union of modules from all of the user’s groups. |
| ProfileID | The account / profile context. Required on requests when the integration has access to multiple profiles. |

 
### Operations Summary
| Operation | Endpoint | Method | Notes |
|-----------|----------|--------|-------|
| List Users | /v1/users | GET | Paged; supports advanced search. |
| Get User By ID | /v1/users/{id} | GET | Retrieves full detail of a single user. |
| Create User | /v1/users | POST | Requires FirstName, LastName, LoginName, and non-empty GroupIDs. |
| Patch User (Partial Update) | /v1/users/{id} | PATCH | Only provided properties are considered; empty string validation rules apply. |
| Replace All Groups | /v1/users/{id}/groups | PUT | Replaces entire membership; at least one GroupID required. |
| Remove Subset of Groups | /v1/users/{id}/groups | DELETE | Removes specified groups; cannot remove all. |
| Disable / Schedule Disable | /v1/users/{id}/disable | POST | With DisableOnDate schedules; without date disables now (if not already). |
| List Modules For User In Group | /v1/users/{userId}/groups/{groupId}/modules | GET | Paged list of security modules tied to that specific group membership. |
| List Groups | /v1/groups | GET | Paged; supports advanced search. Returns (at most) first 10 modules per group in bulk listing. |
| Get Group By ID | /v1/groups/{id} | GET | Full group detail including modules (no 10-module truncation restriction when single fetch). |
 
### User Fields (Selected)
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| UserID | Numeric identifier (read-only). |
| LoginName | Unique login/username. Required on create; cannot be empty on update. |
| FirstName / LastName | Required on create; cannot be set to empty. |
| CorrespondenceEmailAddress | Communication email. Defaults to LoginName if not provided at creation. |
| PhoneNumber | Optional; can be cleared by PATCH with empty string. |
| BillingAccess | Boolean controlling billing visibility. |
| EnableSAMLDirectLogin | Boolean enabling direct SAML login. |
| Status | Active or Disabled. Derived by system when disabling. |
| DisabledOnDate | Nullable date/time when the user auto-disables. Can be set explicitly via disable endpoint. |
| Groups | Collection of user groups (GroupID, GroupName, IsAdmin, etc.). |
 
### Group Fields (Selected)
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| GroupID | Numeric identifier (read-only). |
| GroupName | Display name of the group. |
| IsAdmin | Indicates administrative elevated permissions. |
| ParentGroupID | Optional parent group id (nullable). |
| AccountID / AccountName | Contextual account identifiers. |
| Modules | Security modules granted by this group (may be truncated to first 10 in list endpoint). |
 
### Creating a User (HTTP Example)
```http
POST /v1/users?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "FirstName": "Alice",
  "LastName": "Smith",
  "LoginName": "asmith",
  "CorrespondenceEmailAddress": "asmith@example.com",
  "GroupIDs": [100, 200]
}
```
Response: 201 Created with Location header: /v1/users/{newUserId}
 
### Partial Update (PATCH) Example
```http
PATCH /v1/users/42?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "FirstName": "Updated",
  "EnableSAMLDirectLogin": true
}
```
Response: 204 No Content

PATCH Rules:
* Omitted properties are unchanged.
* Empty string for PhoneNumber clears it.
* Empty string for LoginName / FirstName / LastName is rejected (400).
 
### Replace All Groups Example
```http
PUT /v1/users/42/groups?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{ "GroupIDs": [300, 400, 500] }
```
All prior group memberships are removed and replaced. Response: 204 No Content.
 
### Remove Specific Groups Example
```http
DELETE /v1/users/42/groups?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{ "GroupIDs": [300, 400] }
```
Groups 300 and 400 are removed. At least one group must remain afterward or request is rejected.
 
### Disable User Immediately
```http
POST /v1/users/42/disable?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```
Sets Status to Disabled (if not already). Response: 204 No Content.
 
### Schedule Future Disable
```http
POST /v1/users/42/disable?profileid=12000000 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{ "DisableOnDate": "2025-01-31T00:00:00Z" }
```
Stores DisableOnDate; status remains Active until the specified time. Response: 204 No Content.
 
### List Users (Paged) Example
```http
GET /v1/users?profileid=12000000&page=1&pagesize=25 HTTP/1.1
```
Returns a paged result object containing users and paging metadata.
 
### List Groups (Paged) Example
```http
GET /v1/groups?profileid=12000000&page=1&pagesize=25 HTTP/1.1
```
Returns a paged result object containing groups (each with up to the first 10 modules).
 
### Retrieve Modules For User + Group Example
```http
GET /v1/users/42/groups/100/modules?profileid=12000000&page=1&pagesize=50 HTTP/1.1
```
Returns modules (paged) authorized through that single group membership.
 
### Advanced Search (Users)
Supported searchable fields:
* UserID (number)
* Status (string)
* LoginName (string)
* DisabledOnDate (date)
* FirstName (string)
* LastName (string)
* CorrespondenceEmailAddress (string)
* PhoneNumber (string)
* EnableSAMLDirectLogin (boolean)
* BillingAccess (boolean)
* Groups.GroupID (number)
* Groups.GroupName (string)
* Groups.IsAdmin (boolean)

Operators:
* Strings: : for exact, ~ for contains (values in quotes) e.g. FirstName\~"Ali" or LoginName:"asmith"; negate with leading - (e.g. -FirstName\~"Ali").
* Numbers / Dates: =, >, >=, <, <=
* Booleans: : with "true" / "false" (quoted) e.g. BillingAccess:"true"; negate with leading -.
* Null checks: Field:null or -Field:null (is null / is not null).
* Combine with AND or OR (case-insensitive).

Example:
```http
GET /v1/users?profileid=12000000&search=FirstName~"Ali" AND -Status:"Disabled"&page=1&pagesize=50 HTTP/1.1
```
 
### Advanced Search (Groups)
Searchable fields:
* GroupID (number)
* GroupName (string)
* ModuleID (number)
* ModuleName (string)
* AccountID (number)
* AccountName (string)
* ParentGroupID (number)
* IsAdmin (boolean)

Operators mirror user search (same syntax for strings, numbers, booleans, null checks, AND/OR combination).

Example:
```http
GET /v1/groups?profileid=12000000&search=GroupName~"Admin" AND IsAdmin:"true"&page=1&pagesize=25 HTTP/1.1
```
 
### Validation & Error Highlights
| Scenario | Code (HTTP) | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-------|
| Invalid page or pagesize | 400 | Must meet numeric constraints. |
| Missing profileid when required | 400 | When caller has access to multiple profiles. |
| Unauthorized profile access | 401 | Caller lacks rights to specified profile. |
| User not found | 404 | When referencing a nonexistent user id. |
| Group not found | 404 | When referencing a nonexistent group id. |
| Empty required field on create | 400 | FirstName, LastName, LoginName, GroupIDs. |
| Empty string for restricted field on PATCH | 400 | LoginName, FirstName, LastName cannot be empty. |
| Groups replace without any GroupIDs | 400 | At least one group required. |
| Removing all groups | 400 | Cannot remove all memberships. |
| Internal processing failure | 500 | Generic error message may be returned. |
 
### Behavioral Notes
* profileid must be supplied whenever the integration can access more than one profile; otherwise it may be optional.
* Bulk listing of groups returns only the first 10 modules per group to limit payload size. Use Get Group By ID for full module list.
* Disable endpoint: Supplying a DisableOnDate schedules; otherwise immediate disable (idempotent if already disabled).
* PATCH semantics: Only provided JSON properties are evaluated; omitted properties are left unchanged.
* Group membership always requires at least one group on the user.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Webhooks deliver real-time notifications to your endpoint when subscribed events occur. A webhook defines a delivery endpoint (HTTPS URL), the set of events to subscribe to, and optional authentication. Key capabilities: - List webhook subscriptions for your integration. - Create a new webhook with selected event types. - Update or delete an existing webhook. - Rotate the signing secret when required. - Retry delivery and retrieve failed events using jobs with tokens. Endpoints overview: - `GET v1/Webhooks` - Retrieve all webhooks for the integration. - `GET v1/Webhooks({id})` - Retrieve a single webhook by ID. - `POST v1/Webhooks` - Create a new webhook. - `PATCH v1/Webhooks({id})` - Partially update a webhook. - `PUT v1/Webhooks({id})` - Update a webhook (treated as PATCH). - `DELETE v1/Webhooks({id})` - Delete a webhook. - `GET v1/Webhooks({id})/RetrieveFailedEvents` - Create a job to retrieve failed events or poll job status with `?token=`. - `POST v1/Webhooks({id})/RetryFailedEvents` - Retry delivery of failed events for a given job token. - `POST v1/Webhooks({id})/NewSigningSecret` - Expire current signing secret and generate a new one. - `POST v1/Webhooks({id})/UpdateAuthentication` - Update the authentication method and related fields. Supported Authentication: | Type | Description | |-----------------------|--------------------| | **Signature Header** | *Always supplied as a header*.
Rithum signs webhook events via a Signature header so you can verify Rithum is sending the request and created the payload. This includes a timestamp and two base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 headers, generated from the webhook's Signing Secret. | | **Basic Authorization** | *Optional to enable*.
Rithum RFC2045-MIME (base-64) encodes a Username and Password value you configure and supplies it with an Authorization header in the webhook response. This allows you to quickly validate Rithum sent the request. | | **Custom Header** | *Optional to enable*.
Rithum supplies the header name and value you configure, and supplies them back as the header and value in the webhook response. This allows you to quickly validate Rithum sent the request. | Notes: - WebhookUri must be HTTPS. If omitted on create and the application has a default, it will be used. - AuthenticationType defaults to SigningSecret when not supplied on create. - Do not send ID or SigningSecret in create or update requests. - Use the returned job token with RetrieveFailedEvents to check status or get the result URL. ## Event Payloads For details on webhook event payload structures and schemas, see the [Webhook Event Payloads](#tag/Guides/Webhooks-Guide/Webhook-Event-Payloads) section in the Webhooks Guide.
